item.title: Rabiul: Target to complete six-lane Dhaka-Sylhet highway by June 2029
item.description:
The government is targeting completion of the Dhaka-Sylhet highway's upgrade to six lanes by June 2029, Road Transport and Bridges, Railways and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam has said.
“We are working with the target of completing the six-lane upgrade and opening the road to the public by June 2029,” he said while speaking to journalists on Saturday afternoon after inspecting the progress of the SASEC Dhaka-Sylhet Corridor Road Development Project in Shashai area of Bijoynagar upazila, Brahmanbaria.
He said land acquisition, construction and other activities under the project were being expedited to meet the target.
According to Rabiul, progress in land acquisition has reached around 56% over the past six months following necessary initiatives. He expressed hope that 100% of the land acquisition would be completed within the next two months.
Physical work on the project is also progressing, although the pace varies among its 13 packages, he said.
“Work on eight of the 13 packages is progressing satisfactorily, while the progress of five packages is not at the expected level,” the minister said.
He said authorities were identifying problems affecting progress and resolving them quickly to accelerate work on the affected sections.
The ministerl said the Dhaka-Sylhet highway is one of the country's important national highways and that its development is significant not only as an infrastructure project but also for the economy, trade, tourism and regional connectivity.
Once completed, the project will make communication between Dhaka and the country's northeastern region faster, safer and smoother, he said.
It will also help accelerate business, trade and economic activities in the region, he added.
The minister acknowledged that ongoing construction was causing temporary inconvenience to people in some sections of the highway.
He said concerned authorities had been instructed to take necessary measures to reduce inconvenience to commuters while expediting the project.
Rabiul also instructed officials and contractors to ensure construction quality, complete the work within the stipulated time and give the highest priority to road safety.
“Necessary measures must be taken to increase the pace of work in sections where progress is slow,” he said, urging all concerned agencies to work in coordination to complete the project on time.
During his daylong visit, the minister inspected the Kanchpur-Narsingdi, Brahmanbaria and Habiganj sections of the SASEC Dhaka-Sylhet Corridor Road Development Project.
He reviewed the progress of work through on-site inspections and provided necessary directions regarding implementation.
Road Transport and Highways Division Secretary Dr Mohammad Ziaul Haque, project officials, officials of the Roads and Highways Department and representatives involved in the construction work were present.

item.title: Dengue: Two more die as 1,232 cases recorded in 24 hours
item.description:
Health officials on Saturday said they recorded 1,232 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts killing at least two persons in the past 24 hours.
“During the period, (of the 1,232) 177 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 194 in Chittagong division, 85 in Dhaka division, 175 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 154 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 258 in Khulna division, 54 in Mymensingh division, 82 in Rajshahi division, 47 in Rangpur division and six in Sylhet division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaughts Bangladesh this year witnessed so far 178 deaths while the disease inflicted 60,379.
The dengue last year claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country.
Besides, the dengue claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: PM heads to New York Monday for first UNGA address with busy schedule
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is set to make his first address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on September 24 as he travels to New York on September 21 for the 81st session of the UNGA, with a packed schedule of high-level meetings and diplomatic engagements.
The prime minister, who will be accompanied by a relatively small delegation, will stay in New York until September 25 and is expected to use the visit to outline Bangladesh's vision for the future and articulate its priorities before world leaders.
The General Debate, the annual high-level meeting of heads of state and government, will run from September 22 to 28, a senior official told UNB, noting that the world leaders use the forum to set out their positions and priorities on major global challenges.
Tarique Rahman's visit comes at a particularly significant moment for Bangladesh at the United Nations.
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman was elected president of the 81st General Assembly in June, making him the second Bangladeshi to hold the position.
The 81st session of the General Assembly is being presided over by Dr Khalilur Rahman. The session opened on September 8 and is being held under the theme "Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All."
Prime minister is scheduled to hold more than a dozen bilateral and high-level meetings on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly (UNGA) during his brief visit to New York.
The meetings are likely to include discussions with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Kuwait’s Crown Prince Sheikh Sabah Al-Khaled Al-Sabah, Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković and Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, diplomatic sources said.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk, UN High Commissioner for Refugees Barham Salih, European Council President António Costa, World Bank President Ajay Banga and Boeing Global President Brendan Nelson are also likely to meet the prime minister.
During the visit, the prime minister will also attend a dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said the prime minister's UNGA address would focus on Bangladesh's new vision and the country's democratic transition and aspirations.
"He will have a very busy schedule in New York," Kobir said, adding that Tarique would hold meetings with world leaders on the sidelines of the General Assembly.
The Rohingya crisis will also feature prominently during the visit, with Bangladesh planning a high-level side event on the issue.
"There will be a high-level discussion or meeting on the Rohingya crisis as part of the visit. It is a major priority for us," Kobir said.
Asked whether the UN Refugee Convention would be discussed, the state minister said the government would focus on the broader Rohingya crisis during the visit.
On the possibility of a meeting between Tarique Rahman and US President Donald Trump, Kobir said such engagements are often finalized at the last moment during major international conferences.
"The primary focus of the prime minister's visit is to address the UN General Assembly," he said, adding that details of the prime minister's sideline meetings would be known in due course.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said the 81st General Assembly would provide Bangladesh with an opportunity to present its national interests, economic potential and development priorities to the international community. "It marks a new journey, a new possibility and a new aspiration," she said.
Shama said the government's "Bangladesh First" foreign policy would guide the prime minister's engagements, with an emphasis on presenting Bangladesh internationally as a democratic, confident and responsible country.
The Rohingya crisis will receive particular attention, she said, with a dedicated session planned during the General Assembly involving the prime minister.
Shama said the crisis had become increasingly complex due to the roles of Myanmar authorities, the Arakan Army, regional actors and competing international interests.
"In fact, the problem has deepened. A regional complication has been created. Without international pressure, resolving this problem will become very difficult," she said.
She called for greater international support for a sustainable solution and urged Bangladeshis abroad and civil-society representatives to help mobilise that support.
"The Rohingya crisis is a big problem for Bangladesh. But it's not Bangladesh's problem. The problem was not created by Bangladesh," she said.

item.title: Trump says CNN, Politico, MS NOW banned from White House
item.description:
US President Donald Trump said Friday he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, accusing them of spreading “fake news” about his administration.
The 80-year-old Republican -- who has long had a fiery relationship with the media -- warned that other outlets could face a similar fate but did not say which ones.
The move by Trump drew immediate accusations that it was unconstitutional and would be thrown out by the courts, while the impacted news outlets said they would not be cowed.
“I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW...and Politico...from the White House as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” Trump said on his Truth Social platform.
Trump did not say what prompted the move but added that “media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States.”
Later in the Oval Office, Trump told reporters: “I think that somebody has a right to keep them away if they’re going to write false stories all the time.”
Asked if any particular stories had sparked the ban, he replied: “It’s really just cumulative stories over the last two years.”
“You get sick of it,” he said. “They purposely write negative news, and they do that because they want to try and diminish the Republicans and a Republican administration.”
US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, a former Fox News host who has brought in tight restrictions at the Pentagon, backed Trump’s new ban and accused the outlets of having “endangered troops” with unspecified stories.
Journalists for broadcasters CNN and MS NOW -- which was until recently known as MSNBC -- and Politico remained on White House premises following Trump’s announcement.
Reporters for the two TV news channels could still be seen broadcasting from their stations on the White House driveway.
CNN said Trump’s ban was an “illegal assault” on US press freedom, adding that its reporting was “fair and accurate” and was protected under the US Constitution.
Politico vowed Friday to “vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them.”
The White House Correspondents Association -- the independent body representing journalists covering the presidency -- said it “stands in defense” of the journalists “who are being singled out for doing their jobs.”
Both of Trump’s White House terms have seen him lash out repeatedly at media whose coverage displeases him.
He has filed multiple defamation suits against news outlets, attacked the press on Truth Social and verbally assaulted several reporters, notably women, including CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins.
But it is rare for US presidents to outright bar news outlets -- although Trump banned CNN reporter Jim Acosta in his first term, a ban which a court subsequently overturned.
Last year, Trump barred The Associated Press from some events because of the news agency’s decision to continue referring to the “Gulf of Mexico” -- and not the “Gulf of America” as decreed by Trump.
It has also put stricter controls on journalists in Trump’s second term, including taking control of which outlets can cover events as part of the “pool” admitted to tight spaces such as the Oval Office and Air Force One.
Trump’s surprise announcement on Friday comes at a time when his approval ratings are at record lows and his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress in November’s midterm elections.
The war in Iran and rising prices, particularly at the gas pump, are among the factors that have contributed to his sinking political fortunes.
Bruce Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, said a ban on the media outlets would be “flatly unconstitutional.”
“The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can’t ban others because it doesn’t like their reporting,” Brown said. “This is textbook viewpoint discrimination and will be quickly struck down by the courts if challenged.”

item.title: DU civic initiative to hold dengue awareness photo hunt
item.description:
The Dhaka University Civic Initiative will hold the “Dengue Free DU Photo Hunt” from September 20 to 25 to raise awareness about dengue, campus cleanliness and safety.
The initiative is being organized under the supervision and patronage of Md Tarikul Islam Tariq, joint general secretary of the central committee of Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal.
Under the theme “Find. Click. Report.”, students will identify potential Aedes mosquito breeding grounds across the campus and highlight them through photographs and information.
Long-standing stagnant water, flowerpots, abandoned materials and other waterlogged areas in residential halls, academic buildings and nearby areas will be prioritized.
Participants will have to photograph potentially risky locations and provide the location, a brief description of the problem and suggestions for keeping the area clean and risk-free in the long term.
They will then have to publish the photographs on their Facebook profiles using the designated hashtags: #FindClickReport, #DengueFreeDUCampus and #DhakaUniversityCivicInitiative.
According to the organizers, the program is a “crowdsourced campus reporting initiative” rather than solely a photography competition.
They said it will help identify potentially risky locations on campus and raise awareness about them.
Winners will be selected based on the combined number of likes, comments and shares on participants’ posts. The relevance of the photograph, significance of the problem, accuracy in identifying the location and suggestions for permanent solutions will also be considered, organizers said.
The first-, second- and third-place winners will receive Tk12,000, Tk8,000 and Tk5,000, respectively.
Participants placing fourth to 10th will receive books and tree saplings, while all participants will receive a “University Hero Certificate.”
Speaking about the initiative, Tarikul Islam Tariq said: “Dengue prevention is not solely the responsibility of the administration; students also have an important role as aware citizens. A photograph or a piece of information can often play an effective role in identifying and preventing potential risks.”
He said: “The main objective of this initiative is to develop a culture of responsibility towards the campus, environmental awareness and civic participation.”

item.title: Higher writ disposal eases High Court case backlog
item.description:
The disposal of writ petitions at the High Court Division has increased significantly this year compared to the number of new writ cases filed, helping reduce the pressure of pending cases.
Attorney General Barrister Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal said judicial discipline and an end to writ petitions filed over personal interests or individual disputes could further reduce the pressure of cases.
"Since assuming office, the incumbent chief justice has been trying to bring discipline to the courts. If judicial discipline can be ensured, the number of writ cases will come down. In my view, when there is discipline in the courts, people ultimately get justice," he told BSS.
According to the data provided by Supreme Court spokesperson Md Shafikul Islam, at the beginning of 2026, the number of pending writ cases in the High Court stood at 127,960. During the first three months of the year, from January to March 31, a total of 4,112 new writ cases were filed, while 2,213 writ cases were disposed of during the period.
"From April 1 to June 30, a total of 4,729 new writ cases were filed with the High Court. However, 9,590 writ cases were disposed of during the three-month period. This means the rate of disposal was more than twice the number of new writ cases filed during the period. By the end of June, the number of writ cases pending with the High Court stood at 124, 999," Shafikul added.
Regarding the more than one lakh writ cases pending with the High Court, Attorney General Barrister Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal said that in many cases, writ petitions are filed in personal interests in the name of public interest litigation (PIL). He said the main purpose of such petitions is often self-publicity.
"Many people go before the media immediately after filing a writ petition, which is undesirable," he said.
The attorney general said, I am noticing another trend where writ petitions are being filed over personal disputes. For example, writ petitions are being filed directly with the High Court over land grabbing, land boundaries and disputes concerning bills and baors. But a writ petition cannot be directly filed with the High Court over a private dispute.
"The law requires an individual to approach the lower court and seek remedy by filing a case there. However, many people are bypassing the established procedure and bringing such cases directly to the High Court. As a result, the number of writ cases in the High Court is increasing," he added.
Under Article 102 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, there are five types of writ petitions that can be filed with the High Court. These are
Writ of Habeas Corpus: This writ can be filed when a person is detained without lawful grounds. In such cases, the High Court may order that the person who has been unlawfully detained or arrested be produced before it.
Writ of Mandamus: If a government official or institution fails to perform a duty that it is legally required to perform, the High Court may direct the concerned authority to carry out that duty.
Writ of Certiorari: If a judicial court or tribunal passes an order unlawfully, the High Court may quash the order.
Writ of Prohibition: If a judicial court or tribunal begins proceedings in a matter beyond its legal jurisdiction, the High Court may direct it to stop the proceedings.
Writ of Quo Warranto: If a person holds a public office without having the legal qualifications to do so, the High Court may examine the legality of that person's holding of the office through this writ.

item.title: Bobby Hajjaj: Student learning outcomes key to primary education success
item.description:
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj has said student learning outcomes should be the primary benchmark for measuring the success of reforms and development initiatives in primary education.
He made the remarks while addressing a dialogue titled “Citizen platform dialogue: How far has the government progressed? A focus on primary education,” organised by the Citizen’s Platform for SDGs, Bangladesh, at Lakeshore Hotel in Gulshan, Dhaka, on Saturday.
Bobby Hajjaj said success in primary education should not be measured solely by project implementation or infrastructure development. Instead, the focus should be on how much students are learning in classrooms and whether reforms are improving learning outcomes.
Referring to the Primary Education Development Program (PEDP), he said significant development had taken place in infrastructure, technology and administrative capacity over the years. However, the overall system now needs to be restructured with greater emphasis on student learning outcomes.
“Constructing buildings is one task, while ensuring a student’s education and learning is another. The two cannot be conflated,” he said, stressing that learning outcomes must remain the core objective of primary education.
The state minister said long-term reforms in teacher management were also under way, alongside efforts to address teacher shortages. The government is working to bring teacher recruitment, career progression, evaluation, training and professional development under an integrated framework.
He said the government was also reviewing primary school schedules, the implementation of the single-shift system and measures to ensure adequate classroom learning time.
Initiatives have also been taken to involve child psychologists and early childhood education experts more effectively in curriculum development, he said.
Bobby Hajjaj said all primary-level educational institutions in the country, including public and private schools, would gradually be brought under an effective monitoring system.
He said the state has a responsibility to ensure the quality of education at all primary-level institutions, including Bangla-medium and English-medium schools, kindergartens and other institutions.
The dialogue was chaired by Dr Debapriya Bhattacharya, distinguished fellow at the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD).
Representatives from civil society and various public and private institutions also participated in the discussion.

Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,053 as five die in 24 hours
item.description:
Five more children have died from measles and measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Saturday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,053.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified four of the latest casualties as suspected and one as a confirmed measles death.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 952, while the number of confirmed deaths rose to 101, as one new confirmed measles fatality was reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the four new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka and Sylhet divisions, with two deaths reported in each. At the district level, the highest number of deaths was recorded in Dhaka district.
A total of 941 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Saturday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 178,666.
During the same period, 79 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 20,474.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 157,556 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 151,395 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

Security beefed up in Dhaka after crude bomb blasts, bus arson incidents
item.description:
Law enforcement agencies have tightened security across Dhaka following several crude bomb explosions and bus arson incidents in different parts of the capital.
More than 200 checkpoints have been set up at key locations, flyovers and entry points, with police conducting searches and paying particular attention to motorcycles.
Police said seven to nine cocktail explosions were reported at different locations in Dhaka on Friday. Several passenger buses were also set on fire. Motorcycles were reportedly used in almost all the incidents, prompting police to focus on them during searches.
DMP Media and Public Relations Division ADC Niaz Mehedi said on Saturday that security had been strengthened on major roads, key intersections and the capital’s main entry points.
“More than 200 checkpoints have been set up across the capital, including on the main routes into and out of Dhaka,” he said.
Police are conducting thorough searches of suspicious vehicles, particularly motorcycles, while special drives are underway across the city to maintain law and order.
Niaz Mehedi said checkpoints and picket duties had been strengthened at key locations. The number of police mobile, foot and motorcycle patrols has also been increased significantly.
DB, CTTC and APBn teams have been deployed to prevent major crimes and acts of sabotage, he said, adding that all DMP units remain on round-the-clock alert to ensure public safety.
Police are also monitoring four major entry routes into Dhaka, with particular attention to motorcycles.
Niaz said general diaries and cases had been filed over Friday’s crude bomb explosions and bus arson. Police are collecting CCTV footage from the scenes to identify and arrest those involved.
Meanwhile, the Special Response Battalion (SRB) set up checkpoints on key roads across the capital from Friday night and increased patrols.
In a separate development, DMP arrested 515 people in 47 cases during drives across Dhaka in the past 24 hours.
Of them, 30 were arrested in Ramna, 34 in Lalbagh, 64 in Wari, 76 in Motijheel, 92 in Tejgaon, 120 in Mirpur, 37 in Gulshan, 46 in Uttara and 16 by the Detective Branch.
Police also recovered two foreign-made pistols, two magazines, 10 rounds of ammunition, three machetes, five knives, remnants of exploded cocktails, 53 iron nails, 94.35kg of cannabis, 11,167 yaba tablets and 121.3g of heroin.
The operation also yielded three bottles of foreign liquor, 20 cans of beer, a private car, five mobile phones and Tk7,200.

item.title: Farmgate secret meeting: 12 placed on 3-day remand over suspected militant links
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Saturday placed 12 people, arrested over suspected militant activities during a secret meeting at Tejgaon College Jame Mosque in Farmgate, on three-day remand.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Arifur Rahman passed the order after a hearing on Saturday. Earlier, CTTC Inspector Akhter Morshed, the investigating officer in the case, sought seven days’ remand for each of the accused. Public prosecutor Azizul Haque Didar confirmed the matter.
During the hearing, the prosecution said the accused had allegedly planned to create instability in the country and recruit people to carry out jihad. Their remand was necessary to identify others involved, the prosecution said.
Defence lawyer Masud-ur Rahman opposed the remand plea and sought bail for the accused.
According to the remand application, the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit learned through intelligence and information technology that several young men had gathered near the Tejgaon Coca-Cola intersection with plans to disrupt public order, spread extremism and carry out a major violent incident.
Police later conducted a raid on May 18 with assistance from Tejgaon and Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police and arrested them.
Police said the arrestees were members of a secret WhatsApp group called “Meetup”, through which they allegedly exchanged extremist messages and communicated on various issues. Investigators alleged that they had gathered to plan subversive activities.
The arrested individuals are Mohammad Shihab Uddin, 32; Marzuk Ahmed, 26; Saifur Rahman Khan, 32; Rashmi Mia, 29; Kamichul Islam, 36; Sajjad Hossain, 22; Afif Ahmed, 20; Mohaiminul Haque, 27; Zauji Chowdhury, 19; Shahadat Hossain, 25; Sakib Ahmed, 26; and Junaid Ahmed, 21.
The CTTC said Shihab Uddin had previously been accused of involvement in extremist activities. A case filed against him under the Anti-Terrorism Act with Palash Police Station in Narsingdi is pending trial. Marzuk Ahmed is also facing a pending case under the Speedy Trial Act with Tejgaon police station.
The investigating officer said the accused needed to be questioned to ensure a proper investigation and uncover the circumstances surrounding the incident.The remand application also sought to recover and examine their mobile phones, SIM cards and other digital evidence, as well as analyse cyber data.
Investigators said they also needed to verify the suspects’ communications on WhatsApp, Facebook, Telegram, Messenger and other social media platforms, identify the alleged planners and accomplices, and trace the sources of funding and financiers of the suspected extremist activities.
The court rejected the bail pleas and granted three days’ remand for each of the 12 accused.

item.title: Iran’s ‘new Hezbollah:’ How powerful are the Houthis now?
item.description:
After recent events in Yemen, a small crowd marched down an Iraqi street holding signs that were almost identical.
The signs said, “death to America” and insulted Saudi Arabia and Israel, with slogans very similar to those used by the Houthi rebel group in Yemen. The men in the Iraqi video are members of one of Iraq’s Shiite Muslim paramilitary groups.
Both the Iraqi paramilitaries and the Houthi group in Yemen are part of what is known as the “axis of resistance” in the Middle East, groups supported by Iran that often act at Iran’s behest. Other members are Hezbollah in Lebanon and Hamas in Gaza.
After the US and Israel began attacking Iran in late February 2026, “axis of resistance” members responded by targeting sites associated with the US or Israel. But up until recently, the Houthi group had remained more or less on the sidelines.
However their latest military campaign, which has seen Houthi fighters take further control of the Yemeni coast and several islands in the Red Sea, “sets up conditions to establish… an axis of resistance-controlled body of water as part of [an] effort to assert control over regional oil exports,” US-based research organization the Institute for the Study of War explained last week.
Iran and the US are already fighting for control over the Strait of Hormuz, another important waterway for oil exports and trade.
In Iran, hardline regime-supporting newspapers published laudatory articles about the Houthis’ territorial gains.
The gains “greatly increased the weight of Sanaa [the Yemeni capital, under Houthi control] as a branch of resistance in the ongoing regional war,” one of Iran’s most conservative newspapers, Kayhan, wrote.
Supporters of the Iranian government have been holding nightly gatherings in major cities across the country since the US-Iran war began and this week, at the 200th such event, crowds chanted “you are my soul, O Yemen!”
This was the kind of praise previously lavished on another “axis of resistance” group, Hezbollah. But Hezbollah’s armed faction, degraded by recent Israeli attacks and the loss of their base in Syria, looks less intimidating these days.
And the Houthis now appear to be doing things that Hezbollah couldn’t — for example, bringing down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet this week using a missile the group said it modified itself. Hezbollah has managed to shoot down large Israeli drones and has targeted fighter jets but never hit any.
Could the Houthis be taking Hezbollah’s place as the potentially most important and possibly even more dangerous force in the “axis of resistance?”
The Houthis haven’t had to fight Israel — they are too far away geographically.
“But I think they [the Houthis] have become more valuable than Hezbollah could ever be,” says Farea al-Muslimi, a research fellow focused on Yemen at UK think tank Chatham House. “Of course, Hezbollah had decades of experience and was the one who built the Houthis’ capacity over years. But the Houthis have now exceeded them.”
The Houthis are “increasingly performing a similar strategic function for Iran [as Hezbollah] and in some respects a more useful one,” confirms Andreas Krieg, a senior lecturer at the School of Security Studies at King’s College London.
“Hezbollah gave Tehran deterrence against Israel from Lebanon. The Houthis give Iran leverage over Saudi Arabia, Israel and global shipping,” he told DW. “So I think their strategic importance to Tehran has risen sharply as Hezbollah has come under much greater pressure.”
Al-Muslimi notes that Houthi leaders, including current chief Abdul Malik al-Houthi, were devoted fans of Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah, killed by Israel in 2024 and seen as a hero because of his organization’s part in forcing Israel to withdraw from Lebanon in 2000.
“You can see how he even tries to imitate Nasrallah in his speeches,” al-Muslimi, who co-founded the Sanaa Center for Strategic Studies, told DW. “And now Abdul Malik al-Houthi has more leverage than Nasrallah ever had.”
Nasrallah was once seen as “the fixer” for the “axis of resistance,” he notes, a leader who acted as a conduit between the different factions, giving orders to Iran-supported fighters in Lebanon, Yemen and Syria.
Al-Houthi is likely moving into that role now, al-Muslimi believes, pointing to the fact that one recent attack on Saudi pipelines actually came from Iraqi axis members.
Unlike with Hezbollah though, there’s still disagreement over exactly how much control Iran has over the Houthis.
A review of press by the Iraq-based outlet Amwaj showed that while Iranian media celebrated Houthi gains as a victory for Iran’s “axis of resistance,” Houthi-run channels were more focused on their own fight against Saudi Arabia, which has set up a blockade on Houthi-controlled territories.
Krieg believes the biggest difference between the Houthis and Hezbollah is autonomy.
“The Houthis… have their own leadership, ideology, domestic constituency and territorial project,” he pointed out. “Tehran can enable them, arm them and benefit from their actions, but it cannot necessarily switch them on and off at will.”
Other observers note that in the past, the Houthis moved ahead with certain military plans despite objections from Iran. Tehran has also denied having anything to do with this latest campaign.
But al-Muslimi isn’t so sure. He says that over the past two years, the Houthis have come a lot closer to Iran. There are regular reports of Iran sending sophisticated weaponry to the Houthis. In July, sources inside Iran told Reuters news agency that Iranian leadership had discussed with the Houthis having them close off the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
“Even as Houthi leaders frame their actions in local terms, their alignment with Tehran appears to have tightened,” Allison Minor, previously the US deputy special envoy for Yemen, said in Foreign Affairs magazine last week.
The one thing everyone does agree on is that the Houthis will be hard to rein in. Past military campaigns by Saudi Arabia, the US and other countries have failed. Sanctions and economic pressure tend not to impact either because the Houthis don’t operate within the international financial system.
The Houthis take a “zero sum approach,” al-Muslimi explains. They collect taxes but don’t pay salaries or provide public services; everything goes towards fighting. The group’s founding father argued that contemporary Muslim societies were too “soft,” and that poverty and hardship are a divine test.
That’s very different from Hezbollah: The Lebanese group also has a political branch at home, and offers social welfare services. It must also carefully balance relationships with other demographic groups in Lebanon.
The Houthis have none of those restraints.
“They don’t care if the Israelis bomb the airport or the US bombs a hospital,” al-Muslimi says. “It actually serves them very well because their ideology is all about martyrdom and sacrifice.”
Which, he suggests, makes them potentially more dangerous than Hezbollah, especially for Yemeni civilians.
“They are a major international threat,” he agrees, “but they’re the biggest threat ever to the idea of a republic and citizenship in Yemen’s history.”

item.title: Syria says Friday blast at military site killed 11
item.description:
Syrian authorities on Saturday said an explosion of unknown origin killed 11 people at a military site in the eastern province of Deir Ezzor the previous day.
“The defense ministry held a funeral procession for 11 of its martyrs, who were killed in an explosion at one of the Syrian Arab Army sites” in Deir Ezzor province, the official Sana news agency said.
The ministry had reported on Friday an explosion at an army site in Deir Ezzor, saying it was under investigation.
Firefighters and rescuers headed to the scene of the explosion, state media reported at the time, without immediately providing any casualty figures.
Several such blasts have previously occurred at arms depots in Syria, which is emerging from more than a decade of civil war following the toppling of longtime ruler Bashar al-Assad in late 2024.
Earlier this month, an explosion at an arms depot in the northwest killed 14 people.
Previously, also in the northwest, a car loaded with ammunition had killed at least five people.

item.title: Methanol-tainted drink kills 48 in Nigeria
item.description:
Nigeria’s food and drug regulator on Saturday said alcoholic concoctions tainted with methanol killed 48 people and sickened 182 in recent weeks.
The deaths occurred in three districts of Nigeria’s southwestern Ondo state after victims consumed the locally brewed mixture, which local media said is known as “Monkey Tail.”
The first cases were reported earlier this month and the toll has gradually been rising.
Authorities have arrested 15 people in connection with production and sale of the drink, the agency said.
The country’s National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) said in a statement that after people bought and consumed locally prepared “alcoholic and herbal concoctions,” “48 deaths and 182 cases have been recorded.”
Laboratory tests showed the presence of “high concentrations of methanol,” a deadly alcohol compound, and the indica strain of cannabis in samples of the suspected concoction, the agency said.
Methanol is highly toxic and causes death by organ failure as well as blindness.
NAFDAC said five people had been made totally blind and two partially lost their sight.

item.title: Google’s Gemini AI carried out cyberattacks, guessed passwords
item.description:
Google’s consumer AI model Gemini hacked multiple systems through guessing login credentials, the company told AFP on Friday, the latest case of rogue AI cybersecurity transgressions, which have generated safety concerns.
The hacks, first reported by the Wall Street Journal, took place in May and were discovered by Google in July.
“In a standard evaluation, the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test,” Heather Adkins, Google’s vice president of security engineering, told AFP in a statement.
“In all three of these instances, the model stopped,” Adkins added, without specifying which organizations were breached.
“We ensured the three entities were made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they’ve now made to their testing processes.”
In July, two OpenAI models escaped the closed environment they were meant to stay in, got onto the internet on their own and broke into the internal systems AI platform Hugging Face.
The incident fed worries that AI giants cannot keep their own models under control, as similar episodes have been reported at Anthropic and China’s Moonshot AI.
“These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly,” Adkins emphasized.

item.title: Saudi capital issues first air raid alert since renewed fighting in Yemen
item.description:
Explosions were heard in Riyadh early Saturday, AFP journalists reported, after Saudi authorities issued their first air raid alert in the capital since fighting returned to neighboring Yemen.
The Houthis have been fighting with Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces since the country’s civil war reignited in July, when the group also declared a maritime blockade on Riyadh and began targeting its ships in the Red Sea.
This is the first time the conflict has reached the capital, further shaking a global economy already rattled by nearly seven months of war between the United States and Iran.
“The area is under a hostile aerial threat,” a message received shortly before 3am (0000 GMT) by residents of the Saudi capital warned, urging them to stay indoors.
AFP journalists then heard two explosions, before the alert was lifted about half an hour later by Saudi Arabia’s civil defense agency.
Saudi Arabia is yet to comment on the threat mentioned in the warnings sent overnight to residents of several regions and has not identified where it originated from.
It comes after Riyadh accused the group of targeting Mecca on Wednesday, denouncing it as a “cowardly terrorist attack” on Islam’s holy city, which welcomes millions of pilgrims each year, both Sunnis and Shias.
The Houthis strongly denied the accusation calling it a “worn-out lie.”
In turn, the group reported dozens of retaliatory strikes carried out daily by Riyadh since their lightning offensive this month to take over the country’s entire Red Sea coast, giving them control over the vital Bab al-Mandab strait.
The war in Yemen broke out in 2014 when the Houthis seized control of the capital Sanaa and other regions, triggering in March 2015 a military intervention led by Saudi Arabia.
The fragile truce reached in 2022 between the warring parties collapsed in July, when the pro-Iranian fighters defied Riyadh’s control of Yemeni airspace by allowing an Iranian aircraft to land in Yemen.
Their recent takeover of the coastline has sparked global concern, with international maritime trade already heavily impacted by Tehran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz since the start of the Middle East war in late February.
The Houthis, for their part, insist there is no threat to shipping in the sea lane -- except for Saudi ships, from the world’s leading crude exporter.
Figures from maritime tracking firm Kpler showed that Saudi exports via the Bab al-Mandab strait had dropped since July, although five loaded ships had passed through in the last week.
The United States, which according to Axios last week refused to strike the Houthis at Saudi Arabia’s request, approved the sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to the kingdom on Thursday.
The sale, worth $24.3 billion, is intended to help Riyadh “deter current and future threats,” the US State Department said.
The UN said Friday that the renewed fighting had displaced more than 112,000 people while nearly 3,000 others had fled across the sea to Djibouti, heaping further misery on an already struggling population.

Muslim Pro alternatives: 5 ad-free prayer and Qibla tools (2026)
item.description:
If you only want the prayer times and the direction, IbadahApp does both from a browser and costs nothing — that is the short answer, and four more options follow it.
The longer answer is why people go looking.
Few Muslim apps have been installed more widely than Muslim Pro, and the friction is well documented: heavy advertising in the free tier, including video ads you cannot skip, and Premium at roughly $12.99 a month or $34.99 a year.
There is also the 2020 episode: Vice reported that location data had reached buyers that included US military contractors, passing through a broker called X-Mode.
The company's position was that it had not sold data directly, and it ended the arrangement. Whichever of those brought you here, the five below are free and carry no advertising.
IbadahApp
IbadahApp
There is no paid tier to run into. No subscription, no in-app purchase, and no advertising slots anywhere on the site — which is worth stating plainly, because the pattern you are leaving behind is one where the tool works and then asks. Checking what time Maghrib is and which way to face are not premium activities, and nothing here is gated, dimmed or preceded by a fifteen-second video. The qibla finder sits on the same footing: there is no tier above it to unlock. What the page does on the first day is what it does a year later.
Moving away from a paid app should not mean accepting a worse compass, and it does not here. The arrow is a live one: it redraws while you move, with the Qibla bearing set beside the direction you are facing right now, and it confirms the alignment when you reach it. That last part is the bit that usually separates a polished app from a free web page — being told you have arrived rather than handed a number and left to work it out. On this list you are not trading that away.
Exporting the month is not locked either. The current month of islamic prayer times is laid out day by day, and you can take it away as a JPG or as copied text — and in the category you are migrating from, exporting a timetable is a fairly standard reason to be shown an upgrade screen. Here it is a button. Save it, send it to whoever asks you every week, and that is the last of it.
The two things you came for also stay together on IbadahApp: Islamic Tools . Prayer times and the Qibla share one screen, the way the all-in-one app you are leaving handled it, and it is worth checking you are not giving that up — plenty of free replacements do one or the other and quietly turn one tool into two. This is a like-for-like swap on that count, not a downgrade dressed up as a saving.
QuranTime
QuranTime
QuranTime is the closest thing here to the app you are leaving, minus the price. It is free, carries no advertising, and puts prayer times, the Qibla direction and Hijri-to-Gregorian conversion in one place; Quran reading and the adhkar are there too, so the parts of a comprehensive app you probably used most are all accounted for.
Choose it if what you liked about Muslim Pro was the breadth. People migrating from an all-in-one tool usually discover that the timetable was never the attachment — it was having the Quran, the dhikr and the calendar in the same habit. QuranTime keeps that shape, which makes it the least disruptive move on this list. You are changing where you open things, not what you do.
The detail that tends to matter most to migrants is weight. It runs in a browser on whatever device you have, needs no installation and takes no storage, and stays responsive on older phones. Anyone coming off an app that has been accumulating updates and cached content for three or four years knows exactly what that is worth — the reason for leaving is often as much about a handset that has slowed down as it is about the subscription. A page does not accumulate.
Inner Light
Inner Light
Inner Light, previously known as Salati, is an Android app that is free outright — no advertising, no subscription. Its Adhan is a full-screen one with five voices to choose between, including the Grand Mosque in Makkah and the Prophet's Mosque, and reminders can be configured per prayer: which sound, or a plain notification, or silence, with a lead time of five to twenty minutes. There is also a Hijri calendar and a home screen widget.
This is the one to take if the notification is what you would actually miss. A web page cannot call you to prayer, and for many people that reminder is the single feature that made an app worth having in the first place. The pairing works neatly: the browser tools above handle the looking-up, and this covers the part only something installed can do.
Sajda
Sajda has gone more than a decade without advertising, funding itself through an optional Plus tier instead. It runs on Android and iOS, carries prayer times with a countdown you can nudge by hand, Quran reading, a dhikr counter and a Qibla with both an animated compass and a map view. Cumulative installs run to roughly 13 million at about 4.8 stars.
Take it if you want a polished, comprehensive app and are not opposed to paying a little for extras, as long as the base experience stays clean. Of everything here it feels most like a finished product rather than a utility. The recurring complaint in reviews is that Adhan notifications sometimes fail to fire — which matters, given that reliable reminders are the reason many people pick an app at all.
Mawaqit
Mawaqit is open source and non-profit, free to users and to mosques alike, with no advertising on either side. Its distinguishing feature is where the numbers come from: individual mosques maintain their own timetables on it, iqamah times included, across thousands of mosques in more than a hundred countries. Web, mobile and even a TV version exist.
It is the right move if you attend one mosque regularly. No calculation, however careful, can tell you when that congregation actually stands up — only the mosque's own listing does, and matching the place you pray is a better definition of accurate than matching a formula. The catch is dependence on sign-ups: where your local mosque has not joined, you drop back to estimated times and the advantage disappears.
If prayer times and the Qibla were genuinely all you used, go to a browser tool and stop paying for the rest. Nothing is installed, nothing expires, and both answers arrive on one screen.
If the Quran, the calendar and the adhkar were part of the habit, pick the browser option that still carries them. That is the migration where nothing gets left behind.
And if it was the call to prayer you would miss, keep something installed for that one job alone. A free app handles the reminder, a page handles everything else, and between them you have replaced a subscription with nothing at all — which is a better outcome than swapping one paid tier for another.

BB caps 7% interest rate on loans for closed industrial, service sectors
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has capped the maximum interest rate at 7% for loans under a Tk20,000 crore pre-financing scheme designed to restart closed industrial and service sector enterprises.
At the same time, a six-month grace period facility has been granted following the disbursement of the loans.
During this grace period, no interest can be collected from the borrower.
Once the six-month grace period ends, interest collection must begin, covering the principal repayment along with the accrued interest from the first two quarters.
The central bank issued these directives in a circular on Thursday (September 17).
The circular noted that the term "Large Industry" used in previously issued relevant circulars and circular letters has now been replaced with the term "Industry."
It further stated that the interest rate at the bank level under this scheme will be a maximum of 4%.
In other words, banks will pay 4% interest to Bangladesh Bank against the pre-financing received.
Payment of interest will commence six months after receiving the pre-financing, which will include the accrued interest for the first two quarters.
At the customer level, including all other charges, the maximum interest rate charged under the scheme cannot exceed 7%.
Additionally, interest collection from the borrower must start six months after loan disbursement.
According to the revised guidelines, banks must pay interest to Bangladesh Bank on a quarterly basis after the grace period ends for the funds drawn under the pre-financing facility.
It added that applications for pre-financing can be made at any point within the scheme's three-year tenure, subject to the availability of funds.
Bangladesh Bank issued these directives under the powers conferred by Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, 1991, and they take effect immediately.

item.title: BBS: Inflation drops for third consecutive month to a 10-month low
item.description:
Following several months of high inflation in Bangladesh, the overall trend of easing price pressures continues.
According to the latest data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS), overall inflation dropped for the third consecutive month to 8.26% in August, marking a 10-month low.
With food inflation also falling into the 7% range, there are indications that price pressures on essential commodities in the market are easing somewhat.
An analysis of BBS data shows that after inflation peaked at a year-high of 9.42% in May, it declined by 1.16 percentage points over the subsequent three months.
In July, overall inflation stood at 8.32%. Within a span of a month, it decreased by 0.06 percentage points in August.
Earlier, in November 2025, inflation was at 8.29%. It then gradually rose to hit its peak in May of this year. In June, it dropped to 9.16%.
The slowing growth rate of food prices played the most significant role in driving down inflation.
According to BBS data, food inflation dropped to 7.02% in August, down from 7.16% in July.
In August of last year, this rate was 7.60%. Rural overall inflation decreased from 8.36% in July to 8.31% in August.
Additionally, urban inflation fell from 8.24% in July to 8.20% in August.
Improvements in the supply situation of essential goods, alongside various policy and fiscal initiatives by the government, are believed to be helping reduce price pressures.
In FY27 budget, tax deducted at source (TDS) has already been reduced on 60 essential items.
Furthermore, initiatives like the Food Friendly Program, Open Market Sales (OMS), and Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB) activities for low-income groups have been strengthened.
At the same time, TCB is taking new steps to supply certain imported essentials collected at lower prices without subsidies to the market.
For the current FY27, the government has set a target to bring overall inflation down to 7.5%.
The August statistics indicate positive progress toward that goal.
However, economists point out that a fall in inflation does not mean absolute product prices are decreasing; rather, it means the rate at which prices rise has slowed down.
Consequently, maintaining this recent downward trend to further ease the actual cost-of-living burden on the general public across both food and non-food sectors remains the primary challenge.

item.title: Brac Bank finances Eskayef to expand insulin production in Bangladesh
item.description:
Brac Bank has extended financing support to Eskayef Pharmaceuticals Ltd., also known as SK+F, to expand its insulin production capacity, supporting greater availability of this essential medicine in Bangladesh and international markets.
One of Bangladesh’s leading pharmaceutical companies, Eskayef has been manufacturing insulin through its long-standing partnership with Danish multinational pharmaceutical company, Novo Nordisk, the world’s leading insulin producer.
The partnership has enabled Eskayef to produce insulin in both vial and Penfill formats, helping ensure access to quality insulin for patients living with diabetes.
As part of its latest expansion, Eskayef is establishing a third insulin vial production line to significantly enhance its production capacity and meet growing demand at home and abroad.
This impactful financing reflects the bank’s commitment to supporting strategic investments in Bangladesh’s pharmaceutical and healthcare manufacturing sectors.
The expansion is expected to contribute to greater availability of insulin while strengthening domestic manufacturing capacity for an essential, life-saving medicine.
Increased local production can also help reduce import dependency and further strengthen Bangladesh’s position as a pharmaceutical manufacturing and exporting hub.
Tareq Refat Ullah Khan, managing director & CEO of Brac Bank, said: “Expanding insulin production in Bangladesh means strengthening local capacity for a medicine that people depend on every day. By financing Eskayef’s expansion, we are helping build greater healthcare self-reliance while supporting the growth of one of Bangladesh’s most important manufacturing industries.”
Brac Bank’s Wholesale Banking portfolio spans readymade garments, textiles, pharmaceuticals, construction, power & energy infrastructure and other manufacturing industries, with financing increasingly directed towards projects that add capacity, strengthen supply chains and support industrial growth in the country.

item.title: Bangla QR payment funds to be credited instantly from October 1
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has instructed that payment settlements through Bangla QR code be reduced to real-time, instantly crediting the merchant's account.
Effective October 1, funds from all transactions completed using Bangla QR must be deposited into the respective merchant's account immediately.
Currently, it takes up to one day for Bangla QR payment funds to settle into a merchant's account. Once the new directive takes effect, this waiting period will end.
The central bank issued these instructions to banks, Mobile Financial Services (MFS), and Payment Service Providers (PSP) on Thursday (September 17).
According to the Bangladesh Bank circular, starting October 1, banks, MFS, and PSPs must place the Bangla QR payment icon in an easily visible and accessible location on their mobile app homepages—specifically at the bottom-center of the homepage, within easy reach of the user's thumb.
Additionally, by October 31, financial providers must introduce a feature enabling payments by uploading an image of a QR code alongside the standard camera scanning option.
By the same deadline, all savings and current account holders, including cardholders, must be provided the facility to make Bangla QR payments via mobile apps.
The central bank stated that these directives aim to make digital transactions via Bangla QR more popular and customer-friendly, as well as to encourage merchants to accept payments through this method.
Industry insiders noted that under the new system, merchants will no longer have to wait until the next day to receive payment funds, granting them quicker access to transact their capital.

item.title: BB modifies conditions for representative directors on bank boards
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has imposed new conditions regarding the appointment of representative directors on the boards of banks.
From now on, to become a representative director of a bank on behalf of a shareholding institution, the individual must be the managing director (MD) or a director of that institution.
At the same time, it has been made mandatory for the nominated person to hold a specified amount of shares under their own name in the respective shareholding institution.
Bangladesh Bank issued a circular in this regard on Thursday (September 17).
According to the new directive, a person nominated as a representative director must hold at least 2% of the paid-up capital under their own name in the case of a listed public limited company.
For non-listed companies, they must hold at least 20% unencumbered shares of the paid-up capital of the respective institution under their own name.
This shareholding must be maintained throughout the entire tenure as a representative director.
Bangladesh Bank stated that these conditions have been imposed to ensure transparency and stability in bank ownership structures, control excessive investments relative to the financial capacity of shareholding institutions, ensure the accountability and role of representative directors, and protect depositors' interests.
The circular states that no company can hold shares in single or multiple banks worth more than its net worth.
If an institution's bank shareholding exceeds the newly prescribed limit, it must be brought down to the specified limit within six months.
The central bank believes this will reduce opportunities for investments that are disproportionate to an institution's financial capacity when taking ownership stakes in banks.
Under the new rules, approval from Bangladesh Bank must be obtained prior to the appointment, re-appointment, or change of a bank's representative director.
When applying for approval, proof of the nominated person's status as a director or MD of the shareholding institution and evidence of their required shareholding in that institution must be submitted.
The new directives must also be followed for the re-appointment or change of representative directors previously appointed to bank boards on behalf of shareholding institutions.
Additionally, Bangladesh Bank has instructed that the contents of the new circular be presented at bank board meetings to inform directors and relevant parties.
Banks have also been asked to notify their officers and shareholders about the matter.
Preventing employees from becoming representative directors
Relevant Bangladesh Bank officials noted that in the past, banks controlled by various business groups saw appointments of representative directors who were merely officers or employees of those groups.
This raised questions regarding the independence, genuine representation of ownership, and accountability of representative directors.
According to them, the new conditions were imposed specifically to ensure that no one can sit on a bank's board as a representative director simply by being an employee or close associate of a business group.
Central bank officials further added that establishing a genuine ownership and interest link between the representative director and the shareholding institution will make it easier to verify whose interests are being represented on the board.
Furthermore, making personal share ownership mandatory for representative directors will increase accountability in board decision-making.

item.title: The US Fed rate hike and how it affects Bangladesh
item.description:
The US Federal Reserve’s decision to raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a range of 3.75% to 4.00%—defying political pressure from US President Donald Trump—signals an aggressive push to curb persistent inflation.
While the move is aimed at taming US price pressures driven by energy shocks from the ongoing Iran conflict, tariff spikes, and high consumer costs, its fallout will extend far beyond Washington.
For frontier economies like Bangladesh, tighter US monetary policy creates a complex, multi-layered economic strain across currency valuation, debt servicing, and bilateral trade commitments.
A rate hike by the Fed instantly strengthens the US dollar against global currencies as global capital flows toward higher-yielding, risk-free US assets—evidenced by 10-year US Treasury yields surging past 5%.
For Bangladesh, a stronger dollar pushes the Bangladeshi taka (Tk) into further depreciation.
As the taka weakens, the local cost of importing essential commodities—such as crude oil, LNG, agricultural inputs, and capital machinery—spikes automatically.
This imported inflation directly erodes purchasing power domestically, frustrating central bank efforts in Dhaka to stabilize consumer price levels.
Higher Fed benchmark rates directly drive up global floating borrowing benchmarks, including the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR).
Bangladeshi commercial banks and private corporations holding dollar-denominated short-term debt, deferred Letters of Credit (LCs), or foreign credit lines will face an immediate increase in interest obligations.
Servicing this foreign debt will demand a higher outflow of US dollars, placing direct stress on Bangladesh Bank's foreign exchange reserves as it attempts to supply dollars to clear import backlogs and debt obligations.
Under bilateral economic arrangements and trade deals, Bangladesh commits to purchasing bulk agricultural products, cotton, machinery, and energy products from the United States to balance bilateral trade accounts.
However, higher US interest rates complicate these purchase commitments in two ways:
The Fed’s rate hike comes against a broader backdrop of escalating trade friction, marked by President Trump’s aggressive tariff policies and retaliatory tariff measures globally.
For Bangladesh’s flagship readymade garments (RMG) industry, the US remains a primary export destination.
The dual pressures of trade tariffs and elevated interest rates create a double-bind:

The road ahead
As Fed Chair Kevin Warsh indicated that further rate hikes remain on the table before the end of the year, Bangladesh’s economic policymakers face a delicate balancing act.
Managing foreign exchange liquidity, mitigating imported inflation, and navigating tight international trade terms will require cautious reserve management and adaptive trade strategies in the months ahead.

item.title: DSCC plans to produce electricity, gas, compost, diesel from recycled waste
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Md Abdus Salam has said plans are underway to recycle waste to produce electricity, gas, compost fertilizer and diesel.
He made the remarks as the chief guest at the inauguration of a “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” at Swarighat on the Buriganga River in Dhaka on Saturday. The program was jointly organized by Bidyanondo Foundation and DSCC.
Abdus Salam said waste should not simply be viewed as garbage but should instead be converted into a resource.
“We are focusing on how we can quickly generate electricity through waste recycling. We believe we will be able to move to the initial stage in this regard within a few months,” he said.
“Then waste will be transformed into a resource. It will no longer be left scattered everywhere. On the one hand, we need to raise public awareness, and on the other, we need to recycle waste to produce electricity, gas, compost fertilizer and diesel. Our activities in this regard are already underway,” he added.
The DSCC administrator said the Buriganga was once the lifeline of Dhaka, but plastic, polythene and other waste now float in the river.
He said the “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” initiative had been launched to raise public awareness about preventing river and environmental pollution and to promote the idea of treating waste as a resource.
“We know that all the problems of the Buriganga will not be solved through today’s initiative. But it will send a message to the public that we want to do this and that we need to do it,” he said.
Calling on citizens to come forward to protect the Buriganga, Abdus Salam said people living along both banks of the river and those conducting businesses dependent on it also had a responsibility to act responsibly.
“The Buriganga has reached a point where failure to protect it will leave a bleak future,” he said.
He said initiatives were also being taken to make the Dhaleshwari, Shitalakkhya, Balu and Turag rivers surrounding Dhaka navigable.
“Necessary steps will be taken to restore the river-based transport system that previously connected Dhaka,” he said.
Abdus Salam said under the “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” initiative, plastic and other waste collected from the river and its banks would be accepted through a designated process.
He said there were plans to gradually expand the initiative to all 75 wards under DSCC.
He added that efforts were underway to launch a pilot project in Kamrangirchar in coordination with Bidyanondo Foundation. The project would explore how waste could be recycled and converted into usable resources.
The DSCC administrator also urged citizens to remain vigilant to prevent dengue.
“Dengue cannot be prevented through city corporation activities alone. Coconut shells, water from air conditioners, stagnant water on rooftops or water accumulating anywhere else must not be allowed to remain. If breeding grounds for mosquitoes can be destroyed, dengue can be prevented to a large extent,” he said.
Speaking as a special guest, Dhaka-7 MP Hamidur Rahman said the initiative primarily aimed to encourage people to collect plastic and other waste lying in and around the river.
“Providing food and essential goods in exchange for waste will raise environmental awareness while also promoting the idea of treating waste as a reusable resource,” he said.
He said the initiative should be continued regularly by involving low-income people living along the river.
“If a designated waste collection point and office are established, it will be possible to collect waste while also meeting the food and essential-goods needs of low-income people,” he added.
Under the “Floating Market in Exchange for Waste” initiative, people can exchange collected waste, after it is weighed, for various essential goods, including rice, lentils, flour, cooking oil, fish, chicken and noodles.

item.title: Dhaka air quality turns ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 13th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality on Saturday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 121 at 9:02am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “unhealthy for sensitive groups”, posing health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
Pakistan’s Lahore, India’s Kolkata and Malaysia’s Kuching occupied the first three spots on list with AQI scores of 179, 171 and 169, respectively.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", and anything above 301 is categorized as "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Passenger held at Chittagong airport with Tk 1.17 crore worth of gold
item.description:
A passenger was detained at Shah Amanat International Airport in Chittagong on Friday after 534 grams of gold, valued at around Tk 1.17 crore, were recovered from his baggage, officials said.
The recovered gold comprised 106 grams of jewellery, 425 grams of gold bars and three grams of gold paste, said Engineer Mohammad Ibrahim Khalil, public relations officer of Shah Amanat International Airport.
The passenger was identified as Mohammad Hasan Murad, 37, from Noajishpur Union in Raozan upazila of Chittagong.
Murad arrived at the airport about 8:45 am on SalamAir flight OV-401 from Muscat. He was stopped as he was leaving the customs hall after completing the initial baggage screening, after members of the airport’s Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI), National Security Intelligence (NSI) and customs intelligence units found his movements suspicious.
A subsequent search of his baggage uncovered the gold, which officials said had been concealed inside the luggage using a special method.
According to airport authorities, the concealment had initially prevented the gold from being detected during routine scanning. A separate physical search by intelligence officials later led to its discovery.
The recovered gold was handed over to airport customs authorities, officials said.
Customs intelligence authorities are taking legal action against Murad over his alleged involvement in the transportation of the gold.
Khalil said airport intelligence agencies, customs intelligence, airport customs and airport authorities were continuing coordinated surveillance to prevent gold smuggling and foreign currency trafficking.
Authorities are also maintaining increased scrutiny of passengers and their baggage when suspicious behaviour is detected, he said.

item.title: Dr Zahid stresses sustainable, long-term healthcare development
item.description:
Social Welfare and Women and Children Affairs Minister Dr A Z M Zahid Hossain on Friday stressed the need for developing a long-term and sustainable healthcare system in Bangladesh, keeping in mind the needs of the next 50 years.
"We will not remain forever, but this country and its people will remain. Therefore, we have to develop the healthcare system in a long-term and sustainable manner, considering the needs of the next fifty years," he said while speaking as the chief guest at a program held at the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases and Hospital (NICVD) in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, marking the 'First Open Heart Surgery Day' and the 'Cardiovascular Surgical Conference of NICVD-2026'.
Dr Zahid said ensuring free emergency healthcare services was the responsibility of the state, while the country's overall financial capacity should also be taken into realistic consideration. He recalled with respect the contributions of renowned physicians and specialists who had worked tirelessly to modernize cardiac treatment in Bangladesh.
The minister also expressed gratitude to Japan for providing technical and technological assistance in developing skilled cardiac surgeons during the early stages of cardiac treatment in the country.
He said the prevalence of heart disease, including congenital heart disease, is increasing day by day in Bangladesh. If these diseases cannot be effectively prevented, they could adversely affect the country's productive workforce in the future.
Dr Zahid said the government had already waived taxes on valves and stents used in medical treatment to keep the cost of cardiac care affordable for ordinary people.
He observed that the expansion of modern healthcare facilities in the country had significantly reduced the tendency of people to go abroad for medical treatment. The government has allocated Tk 1.43 lakh crore for social safety-net programmes to reduce the sufferings of ordinary people and ensure their welfare, he said.
The minister also urged affluent members of society to come forward alongside the government in such humanitarian initiatives.

item.title: Two BNP leaders accused of embezzling Tk3.7 lakh from two schools in Natore
item.description:
Two BNP leaders have been accused of embezzling Tk3.7 lakh from two schools in Singra upazila of Natore after allegedly taking the money in the name of developing their village.
The incident reportedly occurred recently in Sukash union, drawing criticism from locals after it came to light.
The accused are Abdus Sobhan Nayan, former joint convener of Sukash Union BNP, and Azmal Hossain, former president of Ward 3 BNP in the union, according to local sources.
School authorities and locals said the money came from the lease of 36 bighas of land belonging to Belowa High School and Belowa Government Primary School.
In June, the two schools leased out the land for one year through open bidding after making a public announcement. The leases generated a total of Tk6,71,625.
On June 24, 21 bighas of land belonging to Belowa High School were leased to local farmers for Tk3,77,250. Four days later, 15 bighas of land belonging to Belowa Government Primary School were leased for Tk2,94,375.
School authorities said the leaseholders handed over the money after the auctions. At the time, the two BNP leaders allegedly told those present that the money would be used for the development of Belowa village.
The leaders allegedly took Tk2 lakh from the primary school's lease proceeds and Tk1.7 lakh from the high school's proceeds.
They later allegedly divided the Tk3.7 lakh between themselves, according to the allegations.
The incident has sparked strong resentment among teachers, students and guardians of the two schools.
Belowa High School Headteacher Anwar Hossain said the two BNP leaders used their influence to take Tk1.7 lakh from the school's land-lease proceeds.
He said he informed the higher authorities immediately after the incident.
Belowa Government Primary School Headteacher Masud Rana declined to comment.
However, at least 10 teachers and employees of the two institutions, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed the incident. They said income from leasing school land is used for various development activities of the institutions.
“Nothing like this has happened at either school since its establishment,” they said, calling for intervention by the local MP and the administration.
Former Sukash Union BNP president Akhtaruzzaman and former general secretary Habibur Rahman condemned the alleged incident, saying taking school funds in the name of village development and sharing the money under political influence was “very regrettable.”
They said the incident had triggered anger among the school authorities, local residents and political circles.
Another local BNP leader, Hafizur Rahman, alleged that some former Awami League leaders had joined BNP and were engaging in such activities, damaging the party's image.
However, Abdus Sobhan alias Nayan denied taking any money.
“The school's money is with the people of the village. If you can, publish the news,” he said.
Azmal Hossain claimed that using some school funds for the development of local religious institutions was not wrong. However, he denied having any of the money.
Singra Upazila Nirbahi Officer Abdullah Al Rifat said he was aware of the allegation involving Tk3.7 lakh from the land-lease proceeds of the two schools.
“The concerned individuals have been given one week to return the money. Legal action will be taken afterwards,” he said.
