item.title: 180-day review finds gaps in govt action on women, children’s rights
item.description:
A review of the government’s first 180 days has found gaps in implementing its election manifesto commitments on women’s and children’s rights, with speakers calling for stronger political commitment, clearer implementation plans and regular accountability.
The review identified shortcomings in implementation planning, prevention of child marriage and child labor, health financing, inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), protection of marginalized groups and regular accountability.
At the same time, progress was noted in areas including budget allocations, school feeding, health service initiatives, expansion of one-stop crisis centers and disability allowance measures.
The findings were presented at a discussion titled “From Commitment to Implementation: The Government’s 180 Days in Protecting the Rights of Women and Children,” organized by the Coalition for Advancing Equality and Justice at Hotel Lakeshore in Gulshan on Wednesday.
The review covered five areas: education; health and nutrition; protection from violence; climate risk and WASH; and diversity and inclusion.
Presenting the keynote, Wasiur Rahman Tonmoy, Lead for Youth and Social Cohesion at Manusher Jonno Foundation, and Rowshon Akhter Urmee, Gender Justice and Social Inclusion Specialist at Oxfam in Bangladesh, outlined the progress and gaps identified in the review.
They recommended faster action on an anti-discrimination law, stronger measures to prevent child marriage and child labor, curriculum reform, health insurance, inclusive WASH systems, manifesto-based budgeting and regular reviews of progress.
Opening the discussion on behalf of the coalition, Kabita Bose, Country Director of Plan International Bangladesh, said the coalition was formed by seven national and international organizations ahead of the 13th National Parliamentary Election to bring women’s and children’s rights more prominently into political and development discussions.
The coalition had submitted evidence-based recommendations to 14 political parties, she said, noting that women, children, girls and young people often receive less priority in election manifestos.
“Investment in women and children should not be seen as charity, but as a rights-based and strategic development priority,” Bose said.
She said the coalition wanted to work with the government and other stakeholders to review progress, identify gaps and support implementation of the commitments.
Political representation
During the panel discussion, BNP reserved-seat MP Anna Minj said women elected through reserved seats were active and capable, but their direct political representation remained constrained by party structures, nomination barriers, election costs and online harassment.
She said the 33% target for women’s participation had not yet been fully implemented and argued that meaningful inclusion should begin within political parties through greater representation of women and other marginalized groups.
Dr Nazneen Ahmed, Executive Director of the Centre for Policy Dialogue, identified financial capacity, priority setting and governance as key challenges.
“Women need equity, not just equality, because years of policy gaps have kept them behind,” she said.
Nazneen also called for initiatives such as the Pink Bus service to be reviewed after several months to determine whether they were reducing harassment or creating new barriers for women.
Dr Md Shafiqul Islam Masud, Jamaat-e-Islami MP from Patuakhali-2, said women’s and children’s rights required political unity, safe workplaces, improved healthcare, childcare support and faster access to justice.
Many incidents of violence may remain unreported because victims fear retaliation or cannot afford legal action, he said, calling on political parties to take a zero-tolerance position on violence against women and children.
Nusrat Tabassum Jyoti, a reserved-seat MP from the National Citizens Party, said women and children continued to face insecurity at home, in public spaces, online and while seeking justice.
She stressed the need to ensure nutritious food for women and girls from childhood and called for stronger protection against violence, clearer safeguards in cyber laws and measures to address deepfake-based abuse.
Climate vulnerability
Md Shamsuddoha, Chief Executive of the Centre for Participatory Research and Development, said climate change was affecting women and children beyond the immediate impacts of cyclones, river erosion and heatwaves.
He pointed to waterlogging, crop losses, migration, child labor, school dropout and poverty as interconnected consequences of climate vulnerability.
He called for human-centered climate planning, stronger governance of climate finance and greater integration of climate action into national development planning.
Govt response
Speaking as chief guest, State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj thanked the coalition for reviewing manifesto commitments and maintaining public scrutiny of political pledges.
He said democratic politics should be based on merit, public service and people’s trust rather than muscle power.
“We must stop dividing ourselves and work together to build a society where women are recognized not only by family roles of being someone’s daughter, mother or wife, but by their own identity and contribution,” Hajjaj said.
He also said temporary measures such as reserved parliamentary seats and Pink Bus services might remain necessary until equal rights and opportunities were ensured.
However, the ultimate goal should be a society where women could participate safely, directly and with dignity, he said.
Hajjaj said the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education was working to strengthen monitoring of primary schools, madrasas and other educational institutions.
The ministry was also planning to pilot free sanitary supplies and awareness programs for adolescent girls and support education infrastructure in haor and other remote areas, he added.
Anil Pant, Country Director of Oxfam in Bangladesh, delivered the vote of thanks.
The Coalition for Advancing Equality and Justice comprises Breaking the Silence, JAAGO Foundation, Manusher Jonno Foundation, Oxfam in Bangladesh, Plan International Bangladesh, Save the Children in Bangladesh and WaterAid Bangladesh.

item.title: Dengue: Seven more die as 1,753 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Seven more people died of dengue, and 1,753 new patients were hospitalized across the country in 24 hours until 8am on Wednesday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 171 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the deaths, three were reported in Khulna division while one each in Chittagong, Mymensingh, Rajshahi and Rangpur divisions, it said.
Currently, 4,166 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at different hospitals across the country.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 56,916 dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 52,579 have recovered.

item.title: ECNEC approves Tk3,822 crore electric train project
item.description:
The government has approved a Tk3,822 crore project to introduce electric train services on the Dhaka-Narayanganj-Joydebpur route by 2031.
The project was among 12 approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) at a meeting at the Secretariat on Wednesday, chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
The 12 projects involve a total cost of Tk168,780 crore and 40 lakh, including three metro rail projects and the electric train project.
Speaking at a press conference in Agargaon after the meeting, Planning State Minister Jonayed Abdur Rahim Saki said the government plans to expand metro rail services in Dhaka and its surrounding areas, as well as in different regions of the country, to improve the transportation system.
He said project costs have increased due to the devaluation of the dollar.
“If project work is not completed quickly, the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) will change the interest rate on its loans after September,” he said.
Alongside the electric train project, three major metro rail projects were revised or newly approved at the ECNEC meeting.
The projects are Metro Rail Line-5 Southern Route, Metro Rail Line-1 and Metro Rail Line-5 Northern Route.
The total cost of implementing the three projects will be around Tk250,000 crore, according to relevant sources.
Revised cost proposals have been made for MRT Line-1, covering the Airport-Kamalapur route, and MRT Line-5 Northern, covering Hemayetpur-Bhatara. Both projects are being financed by JICA.
Meanwhile, the new MRT Line-5 Southern project, covering Gabtoli-Dasherkandi, received approval. The project will be jointly financed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and South Korea.

item.title: Bangladesh eyes sending skilled workers to Bhutan
item.description:
Bangladesh has expressed interest in supplying professional, skilled and semi-skilled workers for the development of Bhutan’s Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC).
The issue came up during a meeting between Bhutanese Ambassador to Bangladesh Dasho Karma Hamu Dorji and Foreign Affairs State Minister Humaiiun Kobir at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Wednesday.
The Bhutanese ambassador congratulated the state minister after the meeting.
During the discussion, the two sides exchanged views on bilateral issues of mutual interest.
Kobir expressed Bangladesh’s keen interest in contributing to the development of GMC, particularly by supplying professional, skilled and semi-skilled human resources.
Recalling the vision of late president Ziaur Rahman, the state minister also sought Bhutan’s support for reviving the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) in the collective interests of the region and its people.
The Bhutanese ambassador expressed deep gratitude for the warm reception accorded to the King of Bhutan during his brief transit at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on August 26 in the presence of the president of Bangladesh.
He also thanked the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for its support in carrying out his duties.

Shama Obaed: Efforts to continue until convicts brought back from India
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Wednesday said Bangladesh will take all necessary legal and diplomatic steps under existing laws to bring back convicted fugitives including former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and those sentenced to death in the latest verdict.
She said the foreign ministry would initiate the required process with the Indian government once it officially receives all necessary documents related to the verdict delivered on Tuesday.
“Look, this is an ongoing process. I should not and do not wish to comment on the legal aspects,” she told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Tuesday sentenced seven people including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader to death for their roles in suppressing the July 2024 mass uprising through incitement, provocation, attacks and killings.
Regarding the foreign ministry's responsibility, Shama said, “We are taking and will continue to take all necessary steps under existing laws to extradite convicted criminals, including the former prime minister of the fascist government and those sentenced yesterday (Tuesday).”
She said efforts are underway under the extradition treaty to bring back the former home minister, the former prime minister and the killers of martyr Hadi, who are currently detained in India. “Official correspondence is being exchanged,” she said.
“Since the verdict was delivered just yesterday (Tuesday), once we officially receive all the necessary paperwork, we will contact the Indian government through due process to take whatever steps are required,” said the state minister.
The government will certainly take all legal measures needed to bring the accused back to face justice, she added.
Asked whether Bangladesh has received any response from India to its earlier letter seeking the extradition of former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, Shama said diplomatic communication is ongoing. “We have not yet received a definitive answer from India,” she said.
“However, from what we understand, they may have their own internal legal procedures to follow, and they are carrying out that process. These efforts will continue until we successfully bring them back to Bangladeshi soil,” she added.
Indian media outlet The Print claimed that India has not yet given its approval to Bangladesh for the appointment of Asad Alam Siam as Dhaka’s next high commissioner at New Delhi though the process to appoint new high commissioners and ambassadors by Dhaka for various foreign postings began in July.
Asked about media reports in Bangladesh and India, Shama urged the media not to publish such reports without official confirmation.
“I would request everyone not to pay heed to or publish such news reports until an official statement or concrete information is issued by either the Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Government of India,” she said.
On an inter-ministerial meeting held on Tuesday regarding Bangladeshis travelling abroad with forged documents and false information, the state minister said the government is working to streamline the migration process for the large number of Bangladeshis living abroad.
“Ever since the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) formed the government, we have been working on how to streamline and consolidate the migration process for the vast number of Bangladeshi citizens living abroad,” she said.
The state minister noted that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had already taken several initiatives, including opening a dedicated Migration Wing.

item.title: RAB begins operations as Special Response Battalion
item.description:
The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has been dissolved and begun operating as the Special Response Battalion (SRB) under the police, with the new unit starting operations on Wednesday.
RAB chief Ahsan Habib Palash confirmed the development. He said: “A gazette has been published under the name ‘Special Response Battalion (SRB).’”
All RAB activities have been carried out under the name SRB since Wednesday following the change. The new name was also reflected in an invitation letter issued for a press conference.
Meanwhile, the government published the gazette notification of the Special Response Battalion Act, 2026, on Tuesday.
The notification states that once the law takes effect, only those provisions of the Armed Police Battalions Ordinance, 1979, that were incorporated to provide the legal basis for forming RAB will be repealed.
However, the RAB (Court Procedures and Departmental Proceedings) Rules, 2005, issued under Section 14 of the ordinance, will remain in force.
Any departmental disciplinary action or court proceedings against a member of the unit under these rules or any other law or regulation will also remain valid and enforceable.
The SRB law further states that relevant RAB personnel, along with its orders, powers, authority, existing facilities, funds, cash and money in bank accounts, liabilities, contracts, movable and immovable property, account books, registers, records and related documents, will be transferred to and vested in the SRB immediately.
Amid objections from the opposition, Parliament passed a bill on Thursday to establish the SRB as a specialized unit. The government has now published the gazette notification of the law.
In 2003, amendments to the Armed Police Battalions Ordinance provided the legal basis for forming RAB. The force subsequently faced criticism over various activities.
The United Nations, the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances, and domestic and international human rights organizations have at various times recommended the dissolution of RAB in light of its past activities.
On December 10, 2021, the United States imposed sanctions on RAB and 7 serving and former senior officials of the force over allegations of human rights violations.

item.title: Mahdi Amin: Bangladesh now a stable nation for investment
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Adviser and Prime Minister’s Office spokesperson Mahdi Amin has said Bangladesh has gained global recognition as a stable destination for investment.
He also said the government’s assurances on gas pressure to representatives of the business community and media are already showing results, with gas pressure increasing.
Mahdi Amin made the remarks at a special press conference at the Korobi Hall of the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon on Wednesday afternoon.
He said inflation was also showing a positive trend, while prices of essential commodities had declined. He also claimed that diesel prices in Bangladesh were lower than in many other countries.
Highlighting what he described as government achievements, Mahdi Amin said technical education had been made mandatory up to Class VI.
He said initiatives had also been taken to establish a public university in Cox’s Bazar dedicated to research on the blue economy.
He said rooftop gardening programs had been introduced at educational institutions across the country.
Mahdi Amin also said pay scales ranging from Tk20,000 to Tk156,000 had been introduced for government financial benefits, and that legislation on property inheritance had been enacted.
Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Saleh Shibli, Additional Press Secretary Atiqur Rahman Rumon and other relevant officials were present at the press conference.

item.title: Teacher killed in snatching: Motorcycle used in incident recovered, 2 arrested
item.description:
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DB) has arrested two more people in connection with the death of headmistress Ronjina Parveen, 55, who fell from a rickshaw after being pulled by snatchers in front of the South Plaza of the National Parliament House.
Police also recovered the motorcycle allegedly used in the snatching and Ronjina’s handbag.
Md Shafiqul Islam, additional police commissioner of the DB, confirmed the arrests and recoveries on Wednesday.
He said Ronjina’s handbag, along with a bus ticket found inside it, had been recovered. He said further details would be disclosed at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre on Wednesday afternoon.
Earlier, on August 30, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) arrested Md Mosharraf Hossain Poni alias Poni Gazi and his associate Cedric in connection with the case.
At the time, RAB said it had recovered a Yamaha R15 motorcycle from them and claimed that it was the motorcycle used in the snatching.
Following the RAB briefing, however, Mosharraf told journalists that he was not involved in the incident. He also claimed that his motorcycle did not resemble the one used in the snatching.
CCTV footage recorded during the incident showed a blue motorcycle, while the motorcycle recovered by RAB was black and white, raising questions over whether it was the same vehicle.
The latest recovery is expected to clarify the discrepancy.

item.title: Moody's updates Bangladesh’s outlook to ‘stable’
item.description:
Moody’s Ratings has updated Bangladesh’s sovereign outlook from ‘negative’ to ‘stable,’ citing reduced political tension, higher foreign exchange reserves, and historic remittance levels.
In its latest evaluation, Moody’s noted that post-election stability and strong public support for the new government have minimized risks to ongoing reforms. Financial backing from the IMF and other international institutions remains vital.
Moody's had previously lowered Bangladesh’s rating from 'B1' to 'B2' in March 2025 with a negative outlook, pointing to bank asset degradation, high inflation, and sluggish growth.
The long-term issuer and senior unsecured ratings stay at ‘B2,’ while the short-term rating remains ‘Not Prime.’
Banking insiders expect this adjustment to expand foreign credit lines for local banks, aiding trade imports.
Moody’s reported reserves grew to roughly $32.9 billion by mid-2026—covering over four months of imports—up from $21.4 billion in 2024. This recovery was fueled by formal remittance channels, flexible exchange policies, and market-driven currency reforms.
Economic expansion is projected to recover slowly, moving from 3.5% in FY2024–25 to 4.1% in FY2025–26, 4.3% in FY2026–27, and potentially 4.9% in FY2027–28 as industrial output stabilizes.
Inflation is expected to hover around 9%.
The sovereign rating was capped at ‘B2’ due to systemic financial sector vulnerabilities, with non-performing loans (NPLs) hitting approximately 32.8% of total loans.
Addressing these capital deficits to meet international standards could require recapitalization equal to 10% of GDP, placing severe strain on public finances.
However, a 12% annual surge in deposits through March 2026 suggests the sector suffers from structural bad debt rather than liquidity shortages.
Bangladesh's low tax-to-GDP ratio restricts fiscal policy, with debt interest payments consuming nearly 30% of government revenue, even though overall public debt stays manageable.
Additional hazards include energy infrastructure vulnerabilities highlighted by recent LNG terminal disruptions, alongside potential losses in trade preferences and concessional loans as Bangladesh graduates from LDC status.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir stresses stronger global cooperation on health, SDGs
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Wednesday underscored the importance of international cooperation and multilateral partnerships in advancing health and achieving sustainable development goals.
He held a meeting with Dr Ahmed Jamsheed Mohamed, representative of the World Health Organization (WHO), at his office and discussed issues of mutual interest.
During the meeting, the state minister and the WHO Representative discussed matters of mutual interest, with particular emphasis on strengthening cooperation in the areas of public health, health security, disease prevention, and access to essential health services.
He appreciated the WHO’s continued cooperation and support in strengthening the country’s health sector and addressing emerging public health challenges.
The WHO Representative briefed the State Minister on the organization’s ongoing and planned cooperation in Bangladesh including support for health-system strengthening, capacity building, disease surveillance, and preparedness for public health emergencies.
Both sides expressed their commitment to further strengthening collaboration between Bangladesh and the WHO and agreed to continue close coordination on issues of common interest at national, regional, and international levels.

item.title: Complaint filed against 5 over alleged enforced disappearance, murder
item.description:
A formal complaint has been filed with the International Crimes Tribunal against five people, including former CTTC chief Asaduzzaman Miah and Additional Deputy Commissioner Ishtiaq Ahmed.
The complaint concerns the alleged enforced disappearance and murder of Abul Hossain Al Amin, principal of Ibn Masud Madrasa in Chattar, Gazipur.
Rashed Khan, political assistant to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, filed the complaint with the tribunal on Wednesday.
Earlier, the tribunal's investigation agency submitted its report to the prosecution, implicating five people, including then CTTC chief Asaduzzaman, ADC Ishtiaq Ahmed and then police inspector Asaduzzaman Miah.
According to sources familiar with the investigation, a group posing as Detective Branch (DB) police abducted Al Amin from Ibn Masud Madrasa in Gazipur on January 30, 2023. He has not been seen or heard from since.
The investigation report said Al Amin was tortured after being detained and allegedly died from the torture. His body was subsequently dumped in the Dhaleshwari River, according to the report.
The report said the CTTC unit arrested six people from different parts of the country on January 28, 2023. Based on information obtained during remand interrogations, a team led by then CTTC ADC Ishtiaq Ahmed detained Al Amin from the madrasa on January 30.
It was alleged that Al Amin was subjected to physical torture for 18 consecutive days at the CTTC office on Minto Road. He became critically ill and later died at the Central Police Hospital, according to the investigation report.
The report further alleged that the accused sought to conceal his death by dumping his body into the Dhaleshwari River from Tulsikhali Bridge in Keraniganj.

item.title: Teesta erosion leaves several hundred families homeless in northern districts
item.description:
At least 386 houses have been washed away by severe erosion along the Teesta River in five northern districts over the past seven days, leaving hundreds of families homeless.
The erosion has intensified at 113 points in Rangpur, Gaibandha, Lalmonirhat, Nilphamari and Kurigram, according to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB).
Ahsan Habib, superintending engineer of the BWDB Rangpur regional office, said the situation has worsened rapidly in recent days.
“Erosion has intensified at 113 points in the five districts while 386 houses have been washed away in the past seven days,” he said.
He said there was insufficient allocation for erosion-control measures and the matter has been brought to the ministry’s attention.
In Gaibandha’s Sundarganj upazila, erosion has taken a particularly heavy toll on people living along the riverbank in Kapasia Union.
In Singijani and Bhorer Pakhi areas, residents said the river current increased suddenly, causing sections of the riverbank to collapse one after another.
Many families could not save their furniture, rice, clothes and other belongings as their houses collapsed.
Shahidul Islam, a resident of the area, said the erosion was so rapid that people barely had time to move their belongings to safety.
Ahad Mia said families are now facing an uncertain future after losing their homes and land.
Sundarganj Upazila Nirbahi Officer Iffat Jahan Tuli visited the affected areas and assured them of necessary assistance.
Gaibandha BWDB Executive Engineer Shariful Islam said geo-bags are being dumped at vulnerable points as an immediate measure.
“We are monitoring the situation and taking immediate preventive measures. Further steps will be taken based on the situation,” he said.
The erosion has also intensified in Kurigram’s Ulipur and Rajarhat upazilas, where around 80 houses have been washed away in the past week.
Families who have lost their homes are struggling to find safe places for themselves, their children and livestock.
In Lalmonirhat, all five upazilas have been affected by erosion.
BWDB Executive Engineer Sunil Roy said the intensity of erosion is increasing with fluctuations in the river’s water level.
Geo-textile materials have been placed at some vulnerable locations, he said but there was no allocation for permanent erosion-control work.
“As there is no allocation for permanent erosion-control work, there is little we can do beyond taking immediate measures,” he said.
Khuliagachh Union Parishad Chairman Khairuzzaman Badal said erosion is continuing almost every day.
In Rangpur, 53 houses have been washed away in Pirgachha, Kaunia and Gangachara upazilas during the past seven days, said BWDB Executive Engineer Hafiz Uddin.
The affected people said they needed permanent protection rather than temporary relief.
In Nilphamari, hundreds of erosion-hit families are spending their days in open spaces, on embankments or in relatives’ yards.
Many families have no arrangements for cooking and food, while residents said tents and dry food were urgently needed.
Abdul Karim of Char Kharibari said the river has eroded the area six times in two years.
“I have lost two houses to the river. Now I don’t know where to go,” he said.
Atwar Rahman said authorities often took measures only after houses began to collapse, rather than taking permanent steps to protect riverbank communities.

Saudi Arabia says Houthis target Makkah, warn of 'red line'
item.description:
The Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis accused the rebels on Wednesday of targeting Islam's holy city Makkah, sparking outrage across the Muslim world and deepening the conflict roiling the region.
Fresh fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government has dragged in Riyadh, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea.
Last week's lightning offensive saw the group seize control of the entirety of Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital artery for Saudi oil exports as the wider Middle East war chokes off the Strait of Hormuz strategic shipping route.
The Houthis swiftly rejected as a "lie" Riyadh's report that it shot down a drone from the rebels heading towards the Saudi city of Makkah, which attracts millions of pilgrims each year.
"The claims about targeting Makkah are a worn-out lie that has been used before and no longer fools anyone," Hazem al-Assad from the Houthis' politburo wrote on X.
The Saudi coalition vowed retaliation, warning that the security of holy sites was a "red line".
"The security of the Two Holy Mosques and the pilgrims is a red line, and the Joint Forces Command of the Coalition will not hesitate to take the necessary and deterrent measures against the Terrorist Houthi Militia," the coalition said in a statement shared by spokesman Turki al-Maliki on X.
The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation -- a bloc of 57 Muslim countries -- condemned the "heinous" attack.
Saudi Arabia had issued brief alerts on Tuesday over possible attacks in Makkah and across swathes of the kingdom's south, which borders Yemen.
The alerts, including the first one issued in Makkah since the Middle East war erupted in February, came a day after a wave of ballistic missile and drone attacks launched from Yemen wounded 13 people in the kingdom's south.
Fighting flared in July when the Houthis, who have for years controlled swathes of northern Yemen, launched a large-scale offensive against Yemeni government forces.
The conflict in the Arabian Peninsula's poorest country has forced 82,000 people to flee their homes since the start of September, according to the United Nations.
Yemen's permanent representative at the UN, Abdullah al-Saadi, said Yemenis were fighting to restore "national institutions across every inch of their land", and called on the international community to take action against the Houthis.
Yemen's plea came as Saudi Arabia and Egypt called for free navigation in the Red Sea following the Houthi's offensive in the vital waterway.
De facto Saudi leader Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called on Tuesday for "ensuring the freedom and security of maritime navigation" through the Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab -- which links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden, the Egyptian presidency said.
The revival of Yemen's civil war, dormant since 2022, has left Riyadh rushing to respond.
US media reported last week that the Saudi crown prince made a personal request to President Donald Trump for US intervention, but was turned down.
The Houthis have insisted that there is no threat to navigation in the Bab al-Mandab except for Saudi vessels.
Any attacks in the waterway are likely to make it less attractive to shippers.
Disruption in the strait could cause Egypt to feel the pinch too, as the Red Sea serves as the gateway to the Suez Canal, upon which Cairo relies for crucial foreign revenue.
Canal revenues are currently around half of what they were before the Houthis first started attacking Red Sea shipping in 2023, a campaign they said was in solidarity with Palestinians during Israel's war against Hamas in Gaza.
On Tuesday, Qatar warned of dire consequences if Bab al-Mandab was closed, saying it would be "catastrophic for the entire world".
The Houthis have also targeted oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, the world's leading crude exporter, helping push global prices above the $100-a-barrel threshold.
The Saudi-led coalition said it would deal with the attacks "firmly to protect the sovereignty of the Kingdom", and would take "all necessary operational measures to deter this... hostile and extremist approach".
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said Tuesday that Saudi Arabia launched 52 airstrikes on Yemen over the past 24 hours, accusing it of targeting civilian sites, including schools and bridges.
But Riyadh's strikes have failed to reverse the group's gains.
A US military task force is working to enhance intelligence-sharing and planning assistance for Saudi forces as they face attacks, a US official told AFP on Tuesday.

item.title: West Bengal IPS officer transferred after backlash over Islamic greetings
item.description:
A woman IPS officer in India’s West Bengal has been transferred after facing backlash from Hindu nationalist groups for using Islamic greetings such as “Assalamu Alaikum,” “Insha Allah” and “Jazakallah” in a video.
Bushra Bano, an Indian Police Service officer, was serving as additional superintendent of police (ASP) in Kharagpur before being transferred on Monday as deputy commandant of the State Armed Police (SAP), reports The Wire.
Bano had previously worked in Saudi Arabia before returning to India and clearing the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) examination twice.
The controversy began after a video featuring Bano’s use of Islamic phrases circulated on social media. Hindu nationalist accounts criticised her for not using slogans such as “Vande Mataram” or “Jai Hind.”
Controversial broadcaster Sudarshan News subsequently described the incident as “UPSC Jihad”, while an organisation called Hindu Legal Fund filed a complaint against Bano with West Bengal’s home secretary.
Bano was transferred a day after the complaint was filed.
The transfer has drawn criticism from opposition politicians and former bureaucrats.
Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra criticised the move, contrasting it with India’s efforts to project a secular image at the recent BRICS summit.
Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi called for the IPS Association to intervene, alleging that Bano had been targeted by online trolling and criticising the state government for transferring her instead of supporting her.
Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi said Bano’s use of the phrases reflected her personal beliefs and did not undermine her commitment to serving the country.
He said pluralism in a diverse country like India was “not a weakness but a matter of pride.”

item.title: Rumon: Media must be more vigilant to prevent misinformation
item.description:
Additional Press Secretary to the Prime Minister Atikur Rahman Rumon has said misleading narratives are being created among the public through distorted and pieced-together news reports circulated across social media and other media platforms.
“Media outlets must perform their responsibilities with greater caution to prevent misinformation,” he said.
He made the comments at a special press conference held at the Karabi Hall of the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon on Wednesday.
Atikur Rahman said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has always believed in freedom of the media. However, he said media freedom must be accompanied by responsibility and caution in news reporting.
Citing examples of what he described as misinformation, Atikur Rahman said some individuals in a neighbouring country had distorted reports claiming that a temple had been demolished as part of new reform initiatives.
“In reality, the government is carrying out development work at the temple,” he said, adding that similar misinformation was also being spread by some individuals within Bangladesh.
Referring to the prime minister’s previous involvement with the newspaper industry, Atikur Rahman said: “Our prime minister was also associated with a newspaper. Just two days before becoming prime minister, he was the publisher of a newspaper. He believes in press freedom.”
Speaking about the government’s performance, the additional press secretary said only six months had passed since the government took office and that many initiatives would take time to produce visible results.
“Everyone needs to be patient to see the benefits of the government’s initiatives,” he said.
He said the prime minister had been working from morning until evening and that the country’s gas and electricity situation was now largely under control.
“The government is working to ensure comfort and peace in people’s lives. We have to work shoulder to shoulder to build a better Bangladesh,” he said.
Prime Minister’s Adviser and PMO spokesperson Mahdi Amin, Press Secretary Saleh Shibli, Deputy Press Secretaries Zahidul Islam Rony and Sujon Mahmud, and Assistant Press Secretary Nazmul Haque Khan were present at the press conference.

Dhaka ranks 2nd among world's most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked second among the world's most polluted cities on Wednesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 165 at 9:50am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", indicating that pollutant levels had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Malaysia's Kuala Lumpur topped the list with an AQI score of 194.
Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City and Kinshasa of the Democratic Republic of Congo ranked third and fourth, respectively, with AQI scores of 162 and 156.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: International Day of Democracy 2026: Legal, institutional reforms essential to protect democracy
item.description:
Legal and institutional reforms are essential to ensure accountable governance and protect democracy and human rights, speakers said at a discussion organized by Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) in Dhaka on Monday to mark International Day of Democracy 2026.
They also called for limiting excessive executive power and ensuring the independence of state institutions responsible for accountability.
They made the remarks at a discussion titled “Democracy, Human Rights and Accountable Governance”, organized by TIB to mark International Day of Democracy 2026.
The discussion was held at the Meghmala Conference Room of TIB’s Dhanmondi office.
TIB Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman said: “Although new possibilities for democracy have emerged through the leadership of young people and the sacrifices of people from all walks of life, our politics, elections and Parliament have essentially become dependent on 5 factors: money, muscle power, religion, patriarchy and majoritarianism.”
“These are major obstacles to establishing democracy, human rights and good governance. We must move away from a one-sided political culture where ‘the winner takes all’ in governing the state,” he said.
He said that although all political parties represented in Parliament, including the ruling party, had committed in their election manifestos to establishing an accountable system of governance, ordinances that further empower the executive branch had been converted into laws.
At the same time, ordinances aimed at making accountability institutions independent and effective had either been repealed or were gradually being converted into laws in ways that, in practice, kept them under government control, he said.
“Therefore, an enabling environment must be ensured to make institutions such as the National Human Rights Commission, Anti-Corruption Commission and Information Commission independent and effective in ensuring human rights and accountability,” he said.
“Alongside comprehensively revising the law on preventing enforced disappearances, the Cyber Security Act and the SRB Bill, the ordinances concerning judicial independence enacted during the tenure of the interim government must be reinstated immediately,” Iftekharuzzaman said.
“The law-making process cannot remain hostage to the interests of any individual or group. Ensuring accountability requires ensuring the inclusion of all,” he said.
“To fulfill the aspirations for democracy, human rights and accountable good governance, political parties and the bureaucracy must undergo a process of introspection based on the underlying lessons of the July uprising,” he added.
In his address as the chief guest, Adviser to the Prime Minister Mahdi Amin said: “The source of the present government’s power is the people of this country. Democracy has returned through the people’s mandate and support following the end of prolonged authoritarian rule.”
“Genuine democracy is established through free, fair and credible elections. The BNP government is sincerely working to protect freedom of expression and human rights and has adopted a zero-tolerance policy to stop enforced disappearances and killings with state patronage,” he said.
He said: “The July uprising does not belong to any particular party or group; rather, it belongs to the people as a whole. The people are the true owners of the state and power.”
“The government is working with a long-term plan to build an accountable state system and an equitable country and is prepared to positively consider reasonable criticism and recommendations,” he added.
In his speech as the special guest, Barrister Muhammad Nawshad Zamir, MP, chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, said: “Rather than the political identity of those appointed to important positions, the key question should be whether qualified individuals are being selected.”
He said: “Alongside constitutional changes, it is also necessary to change our own thinking and mindset in the interests of the country and its people. Everyone must work together, embracing the slogan ‘Bangladesh First’ to safeguard the national interest.”
Dr Manisha Chakraborty, a member of the Central Committee of the Bangladesh Socialist Party (BASAD), said: “As nearly 60% of the members of the current Parliament are businesspeople, more bills are passed in Parliament to serve business interests than those of the people.”
“Democracy has now become monopolized by business interests — ‘of the businessmen, for the businessmen, by the businessmen’ — rather than the people. It is not possible to protect democratic rights while sustaining a discriminatory system.”
She also said loan defaulters were being protected in the Bangladesh envisioned by the students, workers and people who sacrificed their lives in the July uprising.
Politician and physician Tasnim Jara said: “Elections are not merely a formality held once every 5 years. Justice cannot be established if the oversight institutions responsible for ensuring accountability remain under someone’s control.”
She also said: “Organized disinformation campaigns on social media, including the use of bots to create political bullying and digital violence, are essentially organized crimes. They want to suppress young people in this way.”
“But we must speak up about our rights and remain aware,” she said.
University teachers, students, representatives of the younger generation and other participants at the discussion called for inclusive policies to address the sensitive situation in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.
They also called for ensuring the rights of ethnic and religious minorities and eliminating discrimination in processes such as police verification and the allocation of marks in viva voce examinations for government jobs.

item.title: Govt moves to end repeated road digging in Dhaka
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said the government has taken steps to ensure coordinated implementation of development projects in Dhaka and its adjoining areas to reduce public suffering and traffic congestion.
He said all relevant ministries, departments and agencies have been instructed to coordinate their work and stop repeatedly digging up the same roads.
The minister made the remarks while speaking to journalists after a meeting on measures to ease traffic congestion caused by mega projects in Dhaka at the Home Ministry on Tuesday afternoon.
“We held a meeting with all relevant ministries, departments and agencies to ensure coordinated development work. Our aim is to prevent multiple agencies from repeatedly digging up the same area,” he said.
Salahuddin said various projects are currently being implemented by the MRT, Bangladesh Bridge Authority, Roads and Highways Department, city corporations, WASA, power agencies and other service providers.
He said the agencies have been instructed to coordinate their activities, with meetings to be held every 15 days to review implementation.
“We have given several instructions today. We will meet again after 15 days to see how far they have been implemented,” he said.
Focal points have also been designated at the agencies for regular coordination at the officials’ level, he added. Coordination meetings are also being held among the agencies under the Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority (DTCA).
Referring to public suffering caused by road excavation during the monsoon, the home minister said agencies must stop digging up roads shortly after another agency has completed work and repaired them.
“If the power division completes its work and repairs a road, and then another agency digs it up again for gas work a few days later, this must stop,” he said.
“Works that can be carried out simultaneously should be coordinated and completed together,” he added.
Salahuddin said utility relocation is underway in several areas for MRT construction and stressed the need for coordination among the traffic division and other agencies to prevent development work from causing further congestion.
He also said efforts are underway to improve traffic management using artificial intelligence (AI), which, he claimed, has provided some relief to city residents and improved traffic discipline.
Asked about installing integrated utility ducts or lines beneath roads for gas, electricity, water and other services, he said the relevant agencies would consider the matter as necessary.
“Major changes cannot happen overnight. We have started the work. Hopefully, one day we will be able to move towards such a system,” he said.

Amid the controversy, Abu Tayeb Habildar, a student of the Department of Urdu at Dhaka University and a candidate for the vice-president post in the 2025 DUCSU election, entered the museum on Monday afternoon, broke the frames of Jinnah’s photographs and tore them apart.
Later that afternoon, Arko Barua, organizing secretary of the Dhaka University unit of Bangladesh Chhatra Federation, put up a photograph depicting Ghulam Azam being beaten with shoes in place of Jinnah’s photographs.
Meanwhile, the Dhaka University administration has also taken a firm stance over the display of Jinnah’s photograph.
The administration said displaying photographs of individuals whose presence or legacy conflicts with the Language Movement, the historic Liberation Struggle and the core spirit of Bangladesh’s independence is unacceptable at the university or in the Ducsu museum.

A journalist, referring to a recent media report, said a journalist’s accreditation card had been cancelled without the journalist or their organisation being informed of the reason.

item.title: Zahed: EC must coordinate with govt on local election schedule
item.description:
The Election Commission (EC) will have to coordinate with the government when setting the schedule for local government elections, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Broadcasting Dr Zahed Ur Rahman has said.
He also said the timeline announced by the EC should not be considered the government’s final decision.
The adviser made the comments while answering questions from journalists at the Press Information Department's weekly briefing on Tuesday.
“The Constitution gives the EC the responsibility of conducting presidential and parliamentary elections. Other elections are governed by law. So, for local government elections, the EC will have to proceed in coordination with the government,” he said.
Asked about differences between the government and the EC over the local election schedule, Jahed said there was no reason to view the issue as a conflict.
“The government’s decision is important in this election. The parliamentary election is different, as the EC has its own constitutional mandate there,” he said.
Asked whether the EC had violated the law by announcing a timeline without consulting the government, he said: “I would not say the Election Commission has violated the law. You can ask the EC for an explanation on the matter.”
The government has not yet made a final decision on the election date, he said, adding that preparations and the overall situation would be considered before setting the schedule.
“The elections will definitely be held. There is no confusion about that,” he said.
The adviser also said the upcoming local government elections would not be held under party symbols.
“Different political parties will support candidates, and some have already started announcing potential candidates. So there should be no confusion that the election will be competitive,” he said.
He expressed hope that the absence of party symbols would help restore competition in local elections.

item.title: Govt appoints Khondker Talha as Bangladesh Ambassador to France
item.description:
The government has appointed Khondker Mohammad Talha as Bangladesh’s Ambassador to France on a contractual basis.
The Public Administration Ministry issued a gazette notification on Monday, saying his appointment will be effective from October 3, 2026, to December 31, 2027.
The appointment is subject to the suspension of his unavailed post-retirement leave and related benefits, as well as severance of his employment ties with any other profession, business, or government, semi-government or private institution or organization.
A career diplomat, Talha joined the Bangladesh Foreign Service in 1995. He was first appointed Bangladesh’s Ambassador to France in September 2021.
He has also served as director general of the East Asia and Pacific Wing at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka, deputy high commissioner in London from 2014 to 2018, and chief of protocol from 2012 to 2014.
Among his overseas assignments, Talha served at Bangladesh’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations in New York from 2002 to 2006, where he dealt with the General Assembly’s Economic and Financial Committee, ECOSOC, UN funds and programs, among other issues.
He also served at Bangladesh’s Permanent Mission in Geneva from 2008 to 2011, where he handled UNCTAD and WTO-related issues. He coordinated the LDC Group at the expert level at both UNCTAD and the WTO.
Earlier, he served as deputy chief of mission in Tehran from 2006 to 2008.
During his posting in New York, Talha was elected vice-chair of the UN Commission on Population and Development in 2004. While in Geneva, he served as rapporteur of the 99th session of the Council of the International Organization for Migration in 2010.
Talha holds a master’s degree from the University of Dhaka, an MBA from the Institute of Business Administration (IBA), University of Dhaka, and a master’s degree in foreign affairs and international trade from Monash University in Melbourne.

item.title: Photo exhibition on CHT communities held in Dhaka
item.description:
A photo exhibition featuring the everyday lives, struggles, livelihoods and aspirations of communities in the Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) was held at the National Art Gallery of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy in Dhaka on Tuesday.
Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF) organized the exhibition, titled “Rising Hills, Beyond the Frame: A Photo Voice,” featuring more than 65 photographs produced through its Partnership for Resilient Livelihoods in the Chittagong Hill Tracts (PRLC) project.
The European Union-funded project is being implemented by MJF through 9 local partner organizations across Rangamati, Khagrachhari and Bandarban.
European Union Ambassador and Head of Delegation to Bangladesh Michael Miller said the photographs showed what project documents often cannot capture.
He said the images reflected people gaining greater choices, women and men developing sustainable sources of income, families strengthening their wellbeing, and communities becoming more aware of their rights.
He also said: “The European Union views development cooperation as a way to create conditions in which people can improve their own lives and shape their own futures through stronger capacities, better opportunities and local institutions that respond to people’s needs.”
Dr Mohammad Zakaria, director general of the NGO Affairs Bureau, said the PRLC project goes beyond conventional poverty reduction by helping vulnerable families develop sustainable and climate-smart livelihoods.
He also highlighted the role of women in the process, particularly through expanded economic opportunities and greater participation in decision-making.
UNDP Resident Representative Stephen Rodrigues said photographs provided a deeply human way of connecting people with the lives and experiences of others.
He said the exhibition effectively portrayed the lives, culture, aspirations and hopes of communities in the CHT.
Speaking on behalf of the Nagorikata Civic Engagement Fund, Katharina König said photography could be an important medium for storytelling, civic engagement and representation, particularly for marginalized communities.
UN Women Country Representative Geetanjali Singh congratulated MJF, the European Union and UNDP on the initiative and said it offered important lessons on livelihoods and integrated development. She also appreciated the exhibition’s focus on young women and leadership.
MJF Executive Director Shaheen Anam said the PRLC project aims to help 20,000 households move out of extreme poverty by improving health, nutrition and livelihoods.
She said MJF’s rights-based approach extends beyond economic support to protecting rights and ensuring access to justice when violations occur.
Shaheen Anam also urged the government to prioritize implementation of the unimplemented provisions of the Chittagong Hill Tracts Peace Accord, saying this would help local communities rebuild trust and contribute more fully to the region and the country.
MJF governing board member Nirupa Dewan delivered the vote of thanks at the event.
Alongside the exhibition, 2 case-story publications and a photo catalogue were also unveiled.
The exhibition will remain open to visitors until 5pm on September 16 at the National Art Gallery.

item.title: US judge postpones new visa rules for foreign students, journalists
item.description:
A US federal judge on Monday postponed implementation of a Trump administration policy that would impose stricter limits on how long foreign students and journalists can study or work in the United States.
The preliminary injunction from District Judge Dennis Saylor came one day before the new visa rules from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) were scheduled to take effect.
Under the proposed new rules, foreigners on student visas would be admitted for a maximum of up to four years, after which they would have to apply for an extension. International students were previously allowed to remain for the duration of their studies.
Foreign journalists would be limited to stays of just 240 days, or around eight months, but could apply for extensions of similar duration. Until now they could stay up to five years.
Chinese journalists would get just 90 days, with extensions of 90 days.
A coalition of unions representing universities, teachers and journalists had filed a lawsuit challenging the visa restrictions.
Saylor put implementation of the new DHS rules on hold for now without ruling on the merits of the case and scheduled another hearing for October 2.
But in an accompanying memo, the judge expressed skepticism about the visa restrictions on international students and journalists.
He said the current system has permitted tens of millions of foreign students to come to the United States, resulting in "groundbreaking research in science, medicine, and technology, substantial economic growth, and a host of other benefits."
"Rather than attempt to improve that system, DHS elected to replace it with a new program that will substantially restrict the overall number of foreign students, researchers, professors, and journalists," he said.
The judge said that under the new rules, DHS denials of visa extensions would be "entirely discretionary and unappealable."
"A DHS official -- based on limited and vague criteria, and with no possibility of appeal -- will have the power to cut short the academic, research, or teaching activities of any non-US citizen for no reason or any reason."
Foreign journalists applying for visa extensions would also have "no recourse and no appeal" in the event they are turned down, Saylor said.
"The possibilities for abuse are rampant -- in particular, the obvious likelihood that the visas of foreign journalists who are critical of the government (or, more particularly, DHS officials) will not be renewed," he said.
When it proposed the rule, DHS cited national security grounds, an argument the judge said "borders on the absurd" and was "based almost entirely on a small handful of anecdotes."
The visa restrictions are part of a broader immigration crackdown by President Donald Trump spanning aggressive enforcement operations in major cities as well as new restrictions on legal pathways to citizenship.
The United States welcomed more than 1.1 million international students in the 2023-24 academic year, more than any other country, according to official data.

Measles death toll reaches 1,030, eight more die in 24 hours
item.description:
Bangladesh’s measles death toll has reached 1,030 since March 15, comprising 930 suspected and 100 confirmed deaths, as eight more suspected measles patients died in the latest 24-hour period, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The eight deaths were recorded between 8am on September 13 and 8am on September 14, with four reported in Dhaka division and four in Sylhet division.
No confirmed measles death was recorded during the period.
The DGHS also reported 1,177 new suspected measles cases in 24 hours, taking the cumulative number of suspected cases since March 15 to 172,720.
Another 55 cases were confirmed during the period, bringing the total number of confirmed measles cases to 20,124.
Since March 15, a total of 152,117 suspected measles patients have been admitted to hospitals, while 146,400 have been discharged after treatment.
In the latest 24 hours, 1,148 patients were admitted to hospitals and 1,093 were discharged.
Dhaka division recorded the highest number of new suspected cases in the latest 24-hour period, with 424 cases and four deaths.
Chittagong division reported 278 suspected cases, followed by Sylhet with 150, Barisal with 131, Khulna with 88, Mymensingh with 57, Rangpur with 26 and Rajshahi with 23.
Sylhet recorded the other four suspected deaths reported during the period.
Cumulatively, Dhaka has recorded the largest number of suspected cases since March 15, with 74,120 cases and 419 suspected deaths.
Chittagong has recorded 34,078 suspected cases and 70 suspected deaths, while Barisal has reported 18,851 cases and 57 deaths.
Sylhet has recorded 12,958 suspected cases and 161 suspected deaths, Rajshahi 10,120 cases and 93 deaths, Mymensingh 8,344 cases and 77 deaths, Khulna 11,215 cases and 39 deaths, and Rangpur 3,034 cases and 14 deaths.
Among confirmed measles cases, Dhaka has recorded 12,410 cases and 63 deaths since March 15. Chittagong has recorded 2,711 confirmed cases and 10 deaths, while Barisal has reported 781 confirmed cases and 19 deaths.
Rajshahi and Sylhet have each recorded three confirmed deaths, while Mymensingh has reported two. No confirmed measles deaths have been recorded in Khulna or Rangpur during the period covered by the bulletin.
The DGHS bulletin also provided an update on the 2026 national measles-rubella vaccination campaign.
According to the data, 19,779,130 vaccine doses have been administered against a target of 18,015,064 across the eight divisions, representing 109.8% of the stated target.
Mymensingh recorded the highest divisional coverage at 115.1%, followed by Chittagong at 112.7%, Dhaka at 110.6%, Rangpur at 109.9%, Rajshahi at 108.1%, Khulna at 105.1%, Sylhet at 104.8% and Barisal at 104.5%.
Across the city corporations, 2,074,169 doses were administered against a target of 1,905,950, equivalent to 108.8% coverage.
Gazipur City Corporation recorded the highest coverage at 116.1%, followed by Rajshahi at 115.1%, Dhaka North at 112.5% and Chittagong at 112.2%, according to DGHS data.

item.title: Around 20 million children gets measles vaccines in five months
item.description:
The government has administered measles vaccines to 19,771,720 children across the country in five months under ongoing measles-rubella vaccination programme.
This figure exceeded the initial target of vaccination by about 10%.
When the country witnessed a measles outbreak at the end of March this year, the government swiftly launched an emergency vaccination program on April 5, covering 30 upazilas in 18 districts, in the first phase.
The second phase of vaccination began on April 12 in four major city corporations (Dhaka South, Dhaka North, Barisal, and Mymensingh), and in the final third phase, the ongoing nationwide measles-rubella vaccination drive commenced on April 20, said officials at the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
However, due to the persisting measles outbreak, the government is set to launch another massive vaccination campaign starting on September 26 to prevent the disease.
Initially, the officials said the programme aimed to vaccinate about 18 million children nationwide. But the vaccination coverage surpassed the target due to various government initiatives.
According to data from the DGHS, the government's target was to vaccinate 18,015,064 children against measles and rubella. But, as of September 13, a total of 19,771,720 children received the vaccine.
Data obtained from the integrated control centre for the measles-rubella vaccine shows that 1,110,698 children received the measles-rubella vaccine in Barisal division, while 4,841,924 in Chittagong division, 4,919,913 in Dhaka division, 1,695,779 in Khulna division, 1,530,916 in Mymensingh division, 2,213,197 in Rajshahi division, 20,73,488 in Rangpur division and 1,385,805 in Sylhet division.
Among the city corporation areas, 44,119 children were administered with the vaccine in Barisal city, while 336,870 in Chittagong city, 48,643 in Comilla city, 557,688 in Dhaka north city, 418,972 in Dhaka south city, 206,927 in Gazipur city, 83,697 in Narayanganj city, 96,792 in Khulna city, 62,305 in Mymensingh city, 63,059 in Rajshah city, 82,253 in Rangpur city and 72,349 in Sylhet city.
DGHS Additional Director General Professor Dr Zahid Raihan told BSS that vaccinating children is an ongoing process.
However, he said the announcement to administer measles vaccines to children on a massive scale across the country starting September 26 is an intensified effort by the government.
The primary objective of this programme is to ensure that no child is left unvaccinated, he added.

item.title: State minister: Shyamoli TB Hospital to become national TB institute
item.description:
The 250-bed TB Hospital in Dhaka’s Shyamoli will soon be upgraded to the National Institute and Hospital for Tuberculosis Control, said Primary and Mass Education State Minister and hospital management committee Chairman Bobby Hajjaj.
He said the upgrade would expand facilities for tuberculosis diagnosis, treatment, research and training while strengthening the hospital’s overall capacity.
“Necessary initiatives have been taken to develop the hospital into a modern, integrated and effective institution for tuberculosis control,” he said.
Bobby Hajjaj made the comments as the chief guest at a meeting of the hospital management committee at the hospital’s conference room on Monday.
The state minister said steps would be taken to fill vacant posts for doctors, officials and employees as soon as possible.
Addressing the manpower shortage was essential to improve the quality of services and make the hospital’s operations more effective, he said, adding that the necessary measures would be taken in consultation with the Ministry of Health.
He also said an initiative would be taken to construct a new 500-bed building to expand the hospital’s services and capacity.
Bobby Hajjaj instructed the relevant authorities to remove encroachments from the footpath in front of the hospital to ensure unobstructed movement for patients and the public.
During his visit, the state minister inspected different wards and spoke with patients, attendants, doctors, nurses and other healthcare workers about the hospital’s services and challenges.
He also sought updates on cleanliness, medicine supplies and other facilities and instructed officials to take necessary measures to improve the hospital’s overall services.
“Every patient who comes to a government hospital for treatment must be treated with humanity and responsibility. The hospital authorities must give the highest priority to ensuring that patients do not face any kind of suffering or inconvenience,” Bobby Hajjaj said.
The meeting was chaired by Dr Ayesha Akter, member secretary of the hospital management committee and deputy director of the hospital.
Officials from the Ministry of Health, Directorate General of Health Services and Department of Social Services, members of the hospital management committee, health reporters, doctors, officials and employees of the hospital attended the meeting.

item.title: Verdict in case against Quader, Arafat, 5 others Tuesday
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal is set to deliver its verdict on Tuesday against seven accused, including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader, former state minister for information and broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat, and five others in a case involving alleged crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising in 2024.
A three-member bench of International Crimes Tribunal-2, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, fixed the date on Monday.
The other members of the bench are Judge Md Manzurul Bashid and Judge Nur Mohammad Shahriar Kabir.
Prosecutors Gazi MH Tamim, Faruk Ahmed and other members of the prosecution team were present at the tribunal.
The tribunal had earlier kept the case reserved for judgment after hearing closing arguments from both the prosecution and defence. Tribunal-2 passed the order on August 17.
State-appointed lawyers M Hasan Imam and Ishrat Jahan represented the accused, while prosecutors Mizanul Islam and Gazi MH Tamim represented the prosecution.
Besides Obaidul Quader and Mohammad Ali Arafat, the other accused are Awami League Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, Jubo League President Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, and General Secretary Mainul Hossain Khan Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hossain and General Secretary Wali Asif Enan.
All seven accused are absconding.
On January 22, Tribunal-2 ordered the trial to begin after framing charges against the seven accused. The tribunal took cognisance of the formal charges the prosecution submitted on December 18, 2025.
The prosecution began presenting its closing arguments on August 4.
According to the prosecution, the accused jointly issued directives and made provocative and inciting statements to suppress the July-August movement.
They allegedly held several meetings to plan violence and called on party activists to take to the streets and put up resistance.
The prosecution further alleged that the accused were involved in armed attacks, harsh repression and efforts to control the media in some areas.
It said their actions resulted in killings, attempted killings and widespread violence across the country, which constitute crimes against humanity.

Family alleges medical negligence in infant’s death at Dhaka hospital
item.description:
The family of a nine-month-old infant has alleged that medical negligence led to the child’s death at Padma General Hospital in the capital.
A relative raised the allegation during a Facebook Live session late Sunday night, claiming that no doctor was available when the child’s condition deteriorated in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU).
The hospital, however, denied the allegation, saying the child died of cardiac arrest.
The relatives said nine-month-old Ayan Abdullah was admitted to Padma General Hospital on September 1.
The child’s mother alleged that when his condition worsened while he was receiving treatment in the PICU, repeated attempts to call a doctor went unanswered.
“If a child dies right now—if their breathing stops—what happens to them? The child had developed complications beforehand. My allegation is that this occurred precisely because of negligence in duty,” she said.
The relatives also alleged that no doctor was available near their ward.
“There were no doctors in the vicinity of our ward. We went to the doctors’ room nearby. There are several doctors’ rooms; we checked those too. There wasn’t a doctor anywhere. There wasn’t even a doctor from the NICU present,” they said.
Dr Nazmul Haque, a medical officer at the hospital, said the child died of cardiac arrest. He said the child had remained stable until around 8pm but stopped breathing around 9pm.
Dr Md Atiqul Islam, a consultant at the hospital, said he was informed about the situation during the night.
“I asked if my presence was required, but the hospital told me it wasn’t anything serious,” he said.
Zahirul Islam Anik, an administrative officer at Padma General Hospital, said the allegation could be checked through CCTV footage.
“Whether a doctor was present or not can be verified by checking the CCTV footage. We will investigate the matter. We have doctors and nurses on duty 24 hours a day,” he said.
He denied the allegation of medical negligence.

item.title: Application filed to stay Grameen Kalyan’s Tk666 crore tax verdict
item.description:
An application has been filed seeking a stay on the High Court verdict ordering Grameen Kalyan, an entity owned by Dr Muhammad Yunus, to pay Tk666 crore in tax arrears claimed by the National Board of Revenue (NBR).
The application was filed on Monday with the Chamber Judge Court of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court.
On September 10, the High Court ruled that Grameen Kalyan must pay Tk666 crore in taxes claimed by the NBR.
A High Court bench led by Justice Md Mozibur Rahman Miah delivered the verdict after dismissing a rule issued in response to a writ petition challenging the tax demand.
Barristers Abdullah Al Mamun and Fida M Kamal represented Dr Yunus in court.
Earlier, following the July mass uprising, the High Court had withdrawn, on its own initiative, a verdict ordering Grameen Kalyan to pay the Tk666 crore claimed by the NBR.
The withdrawal order was issued by a bench comprising Justice Mohammad Khurshid Alam Sarkar and Justice Sardar Md Rashed Jahangir. The case records were subsequently sent to the chief justice.
The case was later referred to a new bench for hearing.
Grameen Kalyan had filed two separate writ petitions in 2017 challenging tax demands for the 2012-13, 2013-14, 2014-15, 2015-16 and 2016-17 fiscal years following a reassessment.
The court initially issued a rule after a preliminary hearing. A later High Court bench dismissed the rule, effectively upholding the NBR's tax demands.
Lawyers said the dismissal of the writ petitions means the NBR can now collect the amount from Grameen Kalyan as income tax.

item.title: HC seeks mandatory disclosure of marital history in Kabin Nama
item.description:
The High Court has issued a rule seeking mandatory disclosure of the previous and existing marriages, children and government-issued identification details of both the bride and groom in Kabin Nama (marriage document) to prevent fraud and concealment of information.
A High Court bench comprising Justice Ahmed Sohel and Justice SM Iftekhar Uddin Mahmud issued the rule on Monday.
Supreme Court lawyer Ishrat Hasan filed the writ petition in the public interest.
Advocates Sheikh Omar and Tanzila Rahman Jui represented the petitioner at the hearing.
The secretaries of the Law and Justice Division and the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, and the inspector general of the Directorate of Registration were made respondents to the petition.
The petition said the existing Bangladesh Form No. 1601, commonly known as Form D, does not provide an effective mechanism to disclose and verify the previous and existing marriages of either party, former spouses, marriage and divorce records, children, or ongoing legal obligations such as maintenance and guardianship.
Under the current Kabin Nama, a groom is required to provide certain information about an existing wife and permission from the arbitration council, but there is no requirement to disclose details of all previous marriages, divorces, former wives and children. A similar mechanism to verify a bride’s previous marital history is also absent.
The petition said the lack of mandatory disclosure allows individuals to conceal important information when entering into subsequent marriages, potentially leading to fraud and family disputes. It may also deprive prospective spouses of the opportunity to make fully informed decisions and jeopardise the legal rights of existing spouses and children.
The petitioner sought amendments to the Kabin Nama requiring disclosure and verification of both parties’ previous and existing marriages, children from previous or existing marriages, ongoing maintenance and guardianship obligations, other legal liabilities, and birth registration, National ID or passport numbers.
After the hearing, the court asked why the authorities’ inaction in updating the nikahnama to include such information should not be declared unlawful and why necessary directions should not be issued to amend the relevant form to protect citizens’ family lives and legal rights.

item.title: SP suspended after positive drug test
item.description:
Superintendent of police (TR) AFM Nizam Uddin has been temporarily suspended from government service after his urine sample tested positive for benzodiazepines and amphetamine/methamphetamine.
An order to this effect was issued on Monday through a notification signed by Senior Secretary of the Ministry of Home Affairs Manzur Morshed Chowdhury. The notification was signed on September 10.
According to the notification, Nizam Uddin is currently attached to the office of the Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Rangpur Range. He left Police Headquarters on January 8 to attend the DSCSC-2026 course at Mirpur Cantonment.
During the course, he fell ill on June 7 and was taken to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Dhaka. On the advice of specialist doctors, he underwent a drug test as part of his medical examinations.
His urine sample tested positive for benzodiazepines (BZO) and amphetamine/methamphetamine.
The notification said the test results were contrary to the discipline required for the DSCSC course. Under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, such conduct constitutes misconduct and is punishable under the rules.
In view of this, Nizam Uddin was temporarily suspended from government service with effect from August 31 under the relevant provisions of the rules.
During the suspension, he will be entitled to a subsistence allowance in accordance with government rules. The order, issued in the public interest, took effect immediately.
